### `shopping_mall_products`

Core product catalog entries with name, description, category, and base
price linked to seller.

This table stores the current active state of each product. Every time a
seller modifies the product's name, description, category, or base price,
a new immutable snapshot is created in shopping_mall_product_snapshots to
preserve the historical state. The product in this table represents the
latest version available for purchase. Products can be logically deleted
via deleted_at for compliance and audit purposes, but all past snapshots
remain intact.

This table is referenced by shopping_mall_product_images,
shopping_mall_product_variants, and
shopping_mall_product_snapshot_variants. It does not store variant
details, images, or pricing overrides—all of which are stored in their
respective tables and captured in snapshots.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `seller_id`
  > Seller who owns and manages this product. {@link
  > shopping_mall_sellers.id}.
- `category_id`
  > Primary category this product belongs to. {@link
  > shopping_mall_categories.id}.
- `name`: The current name of the product as displayed to customers.
- `description`
  > The current full description of the product, including features and
  > specifications.
- `base_price`
  > The current base price of the product, before variant-specific pricing
  > overrides.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the product was created in the catalog.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the product was last modified.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the product was logically deleted. NULL means active. Used
  > for soft delete compliance.

### `shopping_mall_product_snapshots`

Immutably preserved versions of product metadata at time of change. Each
snapshot captures the exact state of a product (name, description,
category, base price) whenever a seller or admin makes an edit. Used for
audit trail, legal compliance, and dispute resolution. References live
product and category through foreign keys, preserving historical context.
Never modified after creation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `product_id`
  > Reference to the live product being snapshotted. {@link
  > shopping_mall_products.id}.
- `category_id`
  > Reference to the product's category at time of snapshot. {@link
  > shopping_mall_categories.id}.
- `changed_by_id`
  > Reference to the actor (customer, seller, or admin) who created this
  > snapshot. [shopping_mall_users.id](#shopping_mall_users).
- `version`
  > Sequential integer representing the version number of this snapshot.
  > Starts at 1 for the first snapshot after product creation and increments
  > on every edit.
- `changed_at`
  > Timestamp when this snapshot was created, capturing the exact moment of
  > the product edit.

### `shopping_mall_product_images`

Multiple images associated with each product, trackable by position and
deletion status. Images are managed exclusively through the parent
product entity and do not have independent API endpoints. Each image is
stored as a single record with immutable URL and position ordering.
Deletion is soft-deleted to preserve historical accuracy for product
snapshots.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `product_id`
  > Reference to the product this image belongs to. {@link
  > shopping_mall_products.id}.
- `image_url`: URL path to the stored image file. Immutable once saved.
- `position`
  > Order position of the image in the product's image gallery. Used for
  > display sequence. Minimum value: 0.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the image was first uploaded and recorded in the system.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the image was logically deleted. Null if still active.

### `shopping_mall_product_variants`

Product variants with unique SKU codes, pricing overrides, and stock
quantities. Each variant represents a distinct product configuration
(e.g., color, size) and is linked to a specific product. Variants are
immutable in historical orders through snapshots. This is a primary
entity with independent CRUD operations and direct API endpoints for
sellers to manage.

Relates to: shopping_mall_products (one-to-many). Variants are created,
edited, and deleted by sellers. Each variant has a unique SKC code (SKU)
used for inventory tracking. Stock quantity is updated via inventory_logs
on order, restock, cancellation, or refund.

Cannot be deleted if any order item exists in 'paid' or 'shipped' status.
Must preserve all variant snapshots via
shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots.

Reference: 04-product-management.md, 05-inventory-handling.md,
12-snapshot-principle.md

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `product_id`: The product this variant belongs to. [shopping_mall_products.id](#shopping_mall_products)
- `sku_code`
  > Unique Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) code for this variant. Must be
  > alphanumeric, 3-20 characters. Unique across all variants.
- `price`
  > Optional price override for this variant. If null, uses product's
  > base_price. Must be zero or greater.
- `stock_quantity`
  > Current inventory quantity for this variant. Updated by inventory_logs
  > when order is placed, restocked, cancelled, or refunded.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this variant was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this variant was last updated.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete timestamp. If null, variant is active. If set, variant is
  > deleted and cannot be purchased.

### `shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots`

Immutable snapshots of product variant states (SKU, price) at time of
modification, versioned for audit. Each record captures the exact SKU
code and price of a variant at the moment it was edited by a seller or
admin. Maintains a full history of changes with versioning, enabling
precise reconstruction of product pricing and configuration history for
dispute resolution, compliance, and financial auditing. This table never
updates or deletes records - only appends new versions. All fields are
preserved exactly as they existed at the time of change, including
previous values for comparison.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `product_variant_id`
  > The product variant being snapshot. References the live variant in
  > shopping_mall_product_variants.
- `changed_by`
  > The actor who modified the variant (seller or admin). References
  > shopping_mall_sellers or shopping_mall_admins.
- `version`
  > Sequential version number indicating order of changes. Starts at 1 for
  > first snapshot after variant creation.
- `sku_code`: The exact SKU code of the variant at the time of this snapshot.
- `price`
  > The exact price of the variant at the time of this snapshot, in decimal
  > currency format.
- `previous_sku_code`: The SKU code of the variant before this change. Null for first snapshot.
- `previous_price`: The price of the variant before this change. Null for first snapshot.
- `changed_at`: Timestamp when the variant was modified and this snapshot was created.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this snapshot record was created in database.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp of last update to this snapshot record (always same as
  > created_at due to immutability).

### `shopping_mall_inventory_logs`

Immutable history of all inventory changes: restocks, order deductions,
cancellations, refunds, and manual adjustments. Each record represents a
single atomic change to variant stock quantity, with reason, timestamp,
and optional reference to origin (e.g., order item). This is a pure event
log, not a state table. No modification or deletion is ever allowed.
Query pattern: retrieve all changes for a variant ordered by timestamp
DESC. Used by application layer to calculate real-time stock levels.

This table enforces First Normal Form: every field is atomic. All
relationships are through foreign key variant_id. Never stores product
name, price, or seller info — only variant_id and change.

Examples:
- A customer purchases 2 units → change_quantity: -2, reason: "order",
reference_id: "ord_item_abc"
- Seller restocks 10 units → change_quantity: +10, reason: "restock",
reference_id: null
- Cancellation approved → change_quantity: +1, reason: "cancellation",
reference_id: "ord_item_abc"
- Admin manually adjusts → change_quantity: +3, reason: "adjustment",
reference_id: null

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `variant_id`
  > Reference to the product variant that experienced the inventory change.
  > [shopping_mall_product_variants.id](#shopping_mall_product_variants).
- `change_quantity`
  > The quantity change. Positive for restock or refund, negative for order
  > or depletion. Must never be zero.
- `reason`
  > The business reason for this inventory change. Must be one of: 'restock',
  > 'order', 'cancellation', 'refund', 'adjustment', 'loss'. Defined by
  > business rules in 05-inventory-handling.md.
- `reference_id`
  > Optional reference to the source that triggered this change. For example:
  > order_item_id for order/refund/cancellation, or adjustment_id for manual
  > changes. When null, change was initiated by seller or admin without a
  > direct order reference.
- `notes`
  > Optional descriptive notes about the change, e.g., 'Batch #A123
  > restocked', 'Lost in transit'. Used primarily for internal admin context.
  > Never used for calculation.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this inventory event was recorded. Always in UTC.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when this record was last updated. For audit logs, this is
  > typically identical to created_at since records are immutable.

### `shopping_mall_carts`

Container table that groups a customer's active cart items. Associates
customer with their current cart session. This table does not store
product or variant data - those are stored in shopping_mall_cart_items.
Each customer has at most one active cart.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `customer_id`: Customer who owns this cart. [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers).
- `created_at`: Timestamp when cart was created.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when cart was last modified (e.g., when items were added or
  > removed).

### `shopping_mall_cart_items`

Individual item in a customer's shopping cart, capturing immutable
snapshot data of product, variant, and seller profile as they existed at
the moment of addition to cart. This table ensures that pricing, product
description, variant options, and seller identity are preserved exactly
as the customer saw them, even if those details change later. This table
is a subsidiary entity — it has no independent existence outside the cart
context and is automatically consumed during checkout to create order
items. No user interacts with cart items directly; they are always
managed through the cart container (shopping_mall_carts).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `customer_id`
  > Reference to the customer who added this item to cart. {@link
  > shopping_mall_customers.id}.
- `variant_id`
  > Reference to the product variant at time of addition. {@link
  > shopping_mall_product_variants.id}.
- `product_snapshot_id`
  > Immutable snapshot of the product state (name, description, category,
  > base price, images) as it appeared at time of cart addition. {@link
  > shopping_mall_product_snapshots.id}.
- `variant_snapshot_id`
  > Immutable snapshot of the variant state (SKU, price override) as it
  > appeared at time of cart addition. {@link
  > shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots.id}.
- `seller_id`
  > Reference to the seller who listed the product at time of cart addition.
  > [shopping_mall_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_sellers). This replaces non-existent
  > seller_profile_snapshot_id. Seller name/logo are immutable actor
  > attributes stored in shopping_mall_sellers.
- `quantity`: Number of units of this variant added to cart. Must be ≥1.
- `unit_price`
  > Exact unit price of the variant at the time it was added to cart, copied
  > from snapshot.
- `item_total`
  > Total price for this cart item (quantity × unit_price). Calculated at
  > addition time and preserved for audit.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this item was added to the cart. Always immutable.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this item was last modified (e.g., quantity changed).
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete timestamp. If null, item is still in cart. If set, item has
  > been removed from cart.

### `shopping_mall_orders`

Root record of a completed purchase transaction with fixed pricing and
shipping address snapshot. This is an immutable financial record that
cannot be altered after creation. Order status is derived from its order
items and must be tracked via shopping_mall_order_status_histories. All
product, variant, and seller details are preserved as snapshots in
shopping_mall_order_items and shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots, not
duplicated here. This table serves as the anchor for order-level
reporting, financial reconciliation, and customer order history.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `customer_id`: Customer who placed this order. [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers).
- `shipping_address_id`
  > Customer's shipping address chosen at checkout. Stored as a reference to
  > the customer record, since shopping_mall_addresses does not exist. Per
  > 02-user-actors.md, customer addresses are managed as a collection within
  > shopping_mall_customers. This reference identifies the selected address
  > from the customer's address list, not as direct foreign key to a separate
  > address table.
- `total_price`
  > Total order amount at time of checkout, including tax but excluding
  > discounts. Stored as immutable snapshot value. Never recalculated.
- `status`
  > Current status of the entire order, derived from its order items: paid,
  > shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, partially_completed. Immutable
  > after assignment.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when payment was confirmed and order was created. Always in UTC.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp of last status change to this order, triggered by order item
  > status update. Always in UTC.

### `shopping_mall_order_items`

Individual line items within an order, each linked to immutable product,
variant, and seller snapshots at time of purchase. This table anchors
financial accountability: every price, product description, variant
option, and seller profile shown to the customer at checkout is
permanently recorded here regardless of subsequent edits. No updates
allowed after creation — the snapshot reference ensures audit trail
integrity for disputes, refunds, and compliance. This is a primary entity
with independent CRUD access for administrators to audit, filter by
status, and reconcile inventory.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_order_id`
  > Reference to the parent order this item belongs to. {@link
  > shopping_mall_orders.id}.
- `shopping_mall_seller_id`
  > Seller who listed the product at time of purchase. {@link
  > shopping_mall_sellers.id}.
- `shopping_mall_product_id`
  > Parent product referenced at time of purchase. {@link
  > shopping_mall_products.id}.
- `shopping_mall_product_variant_id`
  > Specific product variant chosen by customer at time of purchase. {@link
  > shopping_mall_product_variants.id}.
- `shopping_mall_product_snapshot_id`
  > Immutable snapshot of product state (name, description, base price) at
  > time of purchase. [shopping_mall_product_snapshots.id](#shopping_mall_product_snapshots).
- `shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshot_id`
  > Immutable snapshot of variant state (SKU, price override) at time of
  > purchase. [shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots.id](#shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots).
- `quantity`: Number of units purchased. Always ≥1.
- `price_at_time_of_purchase`
  > Unit price of variant exactly as it was at time of purchase. Never
  > recalculated. Used for revenue tracking and dispute resolution.
- `status`
  > Current status of this order item. Must be one of: 'paid', 'shipped',
  > 'delivered', 'cancelled', 'refunded'. Defined by 07-order-management.md.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this order item was created at the time of order placement.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of the last status change event for this item.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete timestamp. Only set if item is purged for compliance reasons
  > (never in normal operation).

### `shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots`

Immutable snapshot of product, variant, and seller state captured at the
exact moment of order creation. This record preserves the exact product
name, description, category, base price, and images; variant SKU, option
values, and price; and seller profile name, description, and logo—at the
time of purchase. Used for dispute resolution, audit trails, and legal
compliance, ensuring that all transaction data remains unaltered forever.
This snapshot is referenced by order_item and never updated after
creation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `order_item_id`
  > Reference to the order item that this snapshot belongs to. {@link
  > shopping_mall_order_items.id}.
- `product_id`
  > Product ID as it existed at time of purchase. {@link
  > shopping_mall_products.id}.
- `variant_id`
  > Product variant ID as it existed at time of purchase. {@link
  > shopping_mall_product_variants.id}.
- `seller_id`
  > Seller ID as it existed at time of purchase. {@link
  > shopping_mall_sellers.id}.
- `product_name`: Exact product name as it appeared at the time of purchase.
- `product_description`: Exact product description as it appeared at the time of purchase.
- `category_id`
  > Category ID as it existed at time of purchase. {@link
  > shopping_mall_categories.id}.
- `category_name`: Exact category name as it appeared at time of purchase.
- `base_price`
  > Base price of the product as it existed at time of purchase, in decimal
  > format.
- `thumbnail_image_url`: URL of the primary product image as it appeared at time of purchase.
- `all_product_images`
  > JSON array of all product image URLs as they existed at time of purchase,
  > in order.
- `variant_sku`: Exact SKU code of the variant as it existed at time of purchase.
- `variant_price`
  > Price override of the variant as it existed at time of purchase, in
  > decimal format (nullable if no override).
- `option_values`
  > JSON object containing all option name-value pairs (e.g., {"color":
  > "red", "size": "large"}) as they existed at time of purchase.
- `stock_at_time_of_purchase`: Stock quantity of the variant at the exact time of purchase.
- `shop_name`: Exact shop name of the seller as it appeared at time of purchase.
- `shop_description`: Exact shop description of the seller as it appeared at time of purchase.
- `logo_image_url`: Logo URL of the seller’s profile as it appeared at time of purchase.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this snapshot was created (matches order creation time).
- `snapshot_hash`
  > SHA-256 cryptographic hash of the entire snapshot data for integrity
  > verification.

### `shopping_mall_order_status_histories`

Immutable audit trail of all status transitions for the entire order,
recording who and when each change occurred at the order level. This
table captures every transition (paid → shipped → delivered → cancelled →
refunded → partially_completed) with the previous state, new state, actor
responsible, timestamp, and optional reason for audit and compliance.
Designed to support administrative oversight and dispute resolution per
07-order-management.md.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `order_id`
  > References the parent order that changed status. {@link
  > shopping_mall_orders.id}.
- `old_status`
  > The previous order status before the change. One of: 'paid', 'shipped',
  > 'delivered', 'cancelled', 'refunded', 'partially_completed'.
- `new_status`
  > The new order status after the change. One of: 'paid', 'shipped',
  > 'delivered', 'cancelled', 'refunded', 'partially_completed'.
- `changed_by`
  > Who triggered the status change. One of: 'system', 'customer', 'seller',
  > 'admin'.
- `timestamp`: Exact timestamp when the status change occurred, in UTC.
- `reason`
  > Optional brief reason for the status change, e.g., 'Automatically marked
  > as delivered after 14 days', 'Customer requested cancellation', 'Admin
  > overridden'. Max 500 characters.

### `shopping_mall_shipments`

Represents a physical shipment created by a seller containing one or more
order items. Captures carrier and tracking number at time of shipment
creation. This is a primary business entity allowing independent tracking
and management of physical deliveries. Each shipment links to a single
order and seller, enabling accountability and logistical visibility. The
shipment record is permanent and immutable and does not represent
financial state or inventory changes — those are captured in order and
inventory components.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `order_id`
  > The order that this shipment is fulfilling. {@link
  > shopping_mall_orders.id}.
- `seller_id`
  > The seller who created and shipped this shipment. {@link
  > shopping_mall_sellers.id}.
- `carrier_name`
  > The name of the carrier or courier service handling this shipment (e.g.,
  > FedEx, UPS, local postal).
- `tracking_number`
  > The unique tracking number assigned by the carrier for this shipment.
  > Used by customers to track delivery progress.
- `shipped_at`
  > The exact timestamp when this shipment was created and dispatched by the
  > seller.
- `created_at`
  > When this shipment record was initially created in the system. Matches
  > shipped_at for consistency.
- `updated_at`
  > When this shipment record was last updated. Typically only updated when
  > tracking status is manually synced or corrected.

### `shopping_mall_shipment_items`

Junction table that associates each order item with a specific shipment.
Enforces that each order item belongs to exactly one shipment. This table
does not store any business data, only foreign key relationships to
maintain the 1:1 relationship between order_item_id and shipment_id as
required by the shipping workflow. Every shipment item represents an
order item that has been included in a physical shipment. This table is
immutable after insertion.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shipment_id`
  > References the parent shipment entity. This foreign key defines which
  > shipment this order item belongs to. [shopping_mall_shipments.id](#shopping_mall_shipments).
- `order_item_id`
  > References the order item being shipped. Unique constraint ensures one
  > order item is associated with only one shipment. {@link
  > shopping_mall_order_items.id}.

### `shopping_mall_reviews`

Customer reviews with rating, content, and deletion status. Each review
is tied to a specific order item to enforce eligibility (only delivered
items may be reviewed). Reviews are independently managed entities,
allowing customers to create, edit, and delete feedback, while
maintaining audit trails via snapshots in shopping_mall_review_snapshots.
This table captures the active state of reviews and serves as the source
for display and moderation, with immutable historical records preserved
in the snapshot table.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `customer_id`: Customer who wrote the review. [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers).
- `product_id`: Product being reviewed. [shopping_mall_products.id](#shopping_mall_products).
- `order_item_id`
  > Order item that qualifies this review. Must be linked to a delivered
  > order item. [shopping_mall_order_items.id](#shopping_mall_order_items).
- `rating`: Customer's rating from 1 to 5 (inclusive). Required for review submission.
- `content`: Optional textual feedback provided by the customer.
- `is_deleted`
  > Flag indicating whether the review has been logically deleted by customer
  > or admin. True if deleted, false if active.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the review was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the review was last updated. Updated on edit or deletion.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the review was logically deleted. Nullable; if null,
  > review is active.

### `shopping_mall_review_snapshots`

Immutable historical snapshots of review changes including previous
rating, content, and deletion status, with change timestamps and actor
who made the change. Each snapshot represents a point-in-time state of a
review's content and status (including deletion status). This table
preserves full revision history for audit, dispute resolution, and
integrity verification. New rows are added whenever a review is edited
(up to 500 characters) or deleted, always preserving previous state
values. Related to shopping_mall_reviews via review_id. Read-only for
customers and administrators.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `review_id`
  > Reference to the original review in shopping_mall_reviews. {@link
  > shopping_mall_reviews.id}.
- `rating`: The review's rating (1-5) at the time this snapshot was taken.
- `content`
  > The review's text content at time of this snapshot. Null if review was
  > created with no content.
- `is_deleted`
  > The deletion status of the review at the time of this snapshot (true if
  > deleted at that moment).
- `changed_at`: UTC timestamp when this snapshot was created.
- `changed_by`: Actor who triggered the change: either 'customer' or 'admin'.
- `previous_rating`
  > Previous rating value before this change. Null if this is the first
  > snapshot.
- `previous_content`
  > Previous content value before this change. Null if this is the first
  > snapshot or previous content was null.
- `previous_is_deleted`
  > Previous deletion status before this change. Null if this is the first
  > snapshot.

### `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests`

Customer-initiated cancellation requests for order items, with
pending/approved/rejected status and seller/admin response. Each request
is tied to a specific order item and customer. When approved, triggers
inventory restoration and order item status change to cancelled. Seller
or admin must respond with approval or rejection and reason. All requests
are immutable in their state after creation; changes are recorded in the
snapshot table.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `order_item_id`
  > Reference to the order item for which cancellation is requested. {@link
  > shopping_mall_order_items.id}.
- `customer_id`
  > The customer who initiated the cancellation request. {@link
  > shopping_mall_customers.id}.
- `responder_id`
  > The seller or admin who responded to this request. Null until response is
  > made. [shopping_mall_users.id](#shopping_mall_users).
- `reason`
  > Text explanation provided by customer for requesting cancellation.
  > Minimum 10 characters, maximum 500.
- `status`
  > Current status of the cancellation request: 'pending', 'approved', or
  > 'rejected'. Must be one of these three values.
- `response_reason`
  > Text reason provided by seller or admin when approving or rejecting the
  > request. Only populated when status is 'approved' or 'rejected'.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the cancellation request was created. Immutable.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the request status was last updated, e.g., when approved
  > or rejected.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete timestamp. Requests are never permanently deleted, but
  > soft-deleted if invalid or duplicate.

### `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots`

Immutable snapshots of cancellation request state at each status change,
for audit and historical reference. Captures the exact state of the
cancellation request (reason, status, responder, response reason)
whenever it transitions. All data is preserved forever. This table is
write-once and read-only. Used by administrators and customers to resolve
disputes about cancellation decisions. Every change to a cancellation
request creates a new snapshot, preserving the previous state. Never
updated or deleted.
- Each snapshot corresponds to exactly one cancellation request
- Versioned by chronological changed_at timestamp
- Status transitions: pending → approved/rejected
- Captures responder and reason for rejection/approval
- Does not duplicate product or order data - those are in OrderItem
snapshots

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `cancellation_request_id`
  > References the associated cancellation request. {@link
  > shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.id}.
- `reason`
  > The exact cancellation reason provided by the customer at the time of
  > request.
- `status`
  > The status of the cancellation request at the time of this snapshot. Must
  > be one of: 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected'.
- `responder_id`
  > The ID of the seller or admin who responded to the request. Null if
  > pending.
- `response_reason`
  > The reason provided by the responder when approving or rejecting the
  > request. Null if pending.
- `changed_at`
  > The exact timestamp when this snapshot was created (i.e., when the status
  > changed).
- `changed_by`
  > The actor type that created this snapshot: 'customer' (when request
  > created), 'seller' (when responding), or 'admin' (when overriding).

### `shopping_mall_refund_requests`

Customer-initiated refund requests for delivered order items with 7-day
window. Records status, reason, timestamps, and responder. Immutable
status flow: pending → approved/rejected. Preserves request context for
audit and reconciliation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `order_item_id`
  > The order item for which the refund is requested. {@link
  > shopping_mall_order_items.id}.
- `customer_id`
  > The customer who initiated the refund request. {@link
  > shopping_mall_customers.id}.
- `responder_id`
  > The seller or admin who responded to the refund request. {@link
  > shopping_mall_sellers.id} or [shopping_mall_admins.id](#shopping_mall_admins). Nullable
  > until resolved.
- `reason`
  > The reason provided by the customer for requesting the refund. Minimum 10
  > characters, maximum 500 characters.
- `status`
  > Current status of the refund request. Values: 'pending', 'approved',
  > 'rejected'. Follows approval workflow.
- `response_reason`
  > Optional reason provided by the responder. Required if status is
  > 'rejected'.
- `responded_at`
  > Timestamp when the refund request received a response. Nullable until
  > resolved.
- `created_at`: The creation timestamp of the refund request.
- `updated_at`: The last update timestamp of the refund request.

### `shopping_mall_refund_request_snapshots`

Immutable snapshots of refund requests at time of creation or resolution.
Preserves state for audit, reconciliation, and compliance. Each row
represents a versioned state of a refund request when it was created or
changed (approved/rejected). This table has no direct user interaction —
it is written only by system logic when a refund request is created or
updated.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `refund_request_id`
  > Reference to the parent refund request entity. {@link
  > shopping_mall_refund_requests.id}.
- `version`
  > Incremental version number for this snapshot. Starts at 1 for initial
  > creation and increments on each status change. Used to order historical
  > states chronologically.
- `reason`
  > The customer's reason for request as provided at time of snapshot
  > creation or update.
- `status`
  > The status of the refund request at the time this snapshot was taken.
  > Must be one of: pending, approved, rejected.
- `responder_id`
  > The ID of the actor (seller or admin) who responded to the request. Must
  > be null if status is 'pending'.
- `response_reason`
  > The seller's or admin's reason for approving or rejecting the request.
  > Must be null if status is 'pending'.
- `changed_at`
  > Timestamp indicating when this snapshot was created or updated. Must be
  > the exact moment the state changed (creation, approval, or rejection).
- `changed_by`
  > Actor type responsible for the change that triggered this snapshot. Must
  > be one of: 'customer' (for creation), 'seller', or 'admin'.

instruction:
Design API interfaces for an e-commerce shopping mall platform based on the following specifications:

### Authentication

**POST /auth/customers/signup**
- Request Body: { email: string, password: string }
- Response: { success: true, customer_id: number }
- Errors: 409 (email in use), 422 (invalid email/password)

**POST /auth/customers/login**
- Request Body: { email: string, password: string }
- Response: { token: string, customer_id: number }
- Errors: 401 (invalid credentials)

**POST /auth/sellers/signup**
- Request Body: { email: string, password: string }
- Response: { success: true, seller_id: number }
- Errors: 409 (email in use), 422 (invalid email/password)

**POST /auth/sellers/login**
- Request Body: { email: string, password: string }
- Response: { token: string, seller_id: number, status: 'pending'|'approved'|'rejected' }
- Errors: 401 (invalid credentials), 403 (account not approved)

**PUT /auth/customers/password** (Protected)
- Request Body: { current_password: string, new_password: string }
- Response: { success: true }
- Authorization: Customer JWT
- Errors: 401 (incorrect current password), 422 (weak password)

**PUT /auth/sellers/password** (Protected)
- Request Body: { current_password: string, new_password: string }
- Response: { success: true }
- Authorization: Seller JWT
- Errors: 401 (incorrect current password), 422 (weak password)

**DELETE /auth/customers/account** (Protected)
- Response: { success: true }
- Authorization: Customer JWT

**DELETE /auth/sellers/account** (Protected)
- Response: { success: true }
- Authorization: Seller JWT
- Precondition: No pending orders, no pending cancellations/refunds

### Customer Profile

**GET /customers/me** (Protected)
- Response: { id: number, email: string, display_name: string | null, phone_number: string | null, default_address_id: number | null }
- Authorization: Customer JWT

**PUT /customers/me** (Protected)
- Request Body: { display_name?: string, phone_number?: string }
- Response: { id: number, email: string, display_name: string | null, phone_number: string | null }
- Authorization: Customer JWT

### Address Management

**GET /customers/addresses** (Protected)
- Response: [ { id: number, recipient_name: string, phone_number: string, street_address: string, city: string, state_province: string, postal_code: string, country: string, is_default: boolean, created_at: string, deleted_at: string | null } ]
- Authorization: Customer JWT

**POST /customers/addresses** (Protected)
- Request Body: { recipient_name: string, phone_number: string, street_address: string, city: string, state_province: string, postal_code: string, country: string, is_default: boolean }
- Response: { id: number, recipient_name: string, phone_number: string, street_address: string, city: string, state_province: string, postal_code: string, country: string, is_default: boolean, created_at: string }
- Authorization: Customer JWT
- Validation: Only one default address allowed per customer

**PUT /customers/addresses/{address_id}** (Protected)
- Request Body: { recipient_name?: string, phone_number?: string, street_address?: string, city?: string, state_province?: string, postal_code?: string, country?: string, is_default?: boolean }
- Response: { id: number, recipient_name: string, phone_number: string, street_address: string, city: string, state_province: string, postal_code: string, country: string, is_default: boolean, updated_at: string }
- Authorization: Customer JWT
- Validation: If setting is_default=true, any previous default is automatically unset

**DELETE /customers/addresses/{address_id}** (Protected)
- Response: { success: true }
- Authorization: Customer JWT

### Seller Profile

**GET /sellers/me** (Protected)
- Response: { id: number, email: string, status: 'pending'|'approved'|'rejected', rejection_reason: string | null, shop_name: string | null, shop_description: string | null, logo_image_url: string | null, suspended_at: string | null }
- Authorization: Seller JWT

**GET /sellers/{seller_id}**
- Response: { id: number, shop_name: string | null, shop_description: string | null, logo_image_url: string | null, created_at: string, approved_at: string | null }

**PUT /sellers/me** (Protected)
- Request Body: { shop_name?: string, shop_description?: string, logo_image_url?: string }
- Response: { id: number, shop_name: string | null, shop_description: string | null, logo_image_url: string | null }
- Authorization: Seller JWT
- Side effect: Creates seller profile snapshot

**GET /sellers/me/snapshots** (Protected)
- Query: page? (default 1), limit? (default 20)
- Response: { data: [ { shop_name: string, shop_description: string, logo_image_url: string | null, changed_at: string, changed_by: 'seller'|'admin', previous_shop_name: string | null, previous_shop_description: string | null, previous_logo_image_url: string | null } ], pagination: { page: number, limit: number, total: number } }
- Authorization: Seller JWT

**GET /sellers/{seller_id}/snapshots**
- Query: page? (default 1), limit? (default 20)
- Response: Same structure as above

### Category Management

**GET /categories**
- Response: [ { id: number, name: string, description: string | null, parent_category_id: number | null, created_at: string, updated_at: string, deleted_at: string | null } ]
- Optional Query: parent_id? (filter subcategories)

**GET /categories/tree**
- Response: Recursive structure with parent-child relationship (one level of nesting)

**POST /admin/categories** (Protected)
- Request Body: { name: string, description?: string, parent_category_id?: number }
- Response: { id: number }
- Authorization: Admin JWT

**PUT /admin/categories/{category_id}** (Protected)
- Request Body: { name?: string, description?: string }
- Response: { id: number, name: string, description: string | null, updated_at: string }
- Authorization: Admin JWT

**DELETE /admin/categories/{category_id}** (Protected)
- Response: { success: true }
- Authorization: Admin JWT

### Product Management

**GET /products**
- Query: 
  - search? (text)
  - category_id? (number)
  - min_price? (number)
  - max_price? (number)
  - in_stock_only? (boolean, default false)
  - sort? ('newest'|'price_asc'|'price_desc', default 'newest')
  - page? (default 1)
  - limit? (default 10)
- Response: { data: [ { id: number, name: string, description: string, base_price: number, category: { id: number, name: string }, seller: { id: number, shop_name: string }, main_image_url: string, avg_rating: number | null, review_count: number, variants: [ { id: number, sku_code: string, price: number | null, stock_quantity: number } ] } ], pagination: { page: number, limit: number, total: number } }

**GET /products/{product_id}**
- Response: { id: number, name: string, description: string, base_price: number, category: { id: number, name: string }, seller: { id: number, shop_name: string }, images: [ { id: number, image_url: string, position: number } ], variants: [ { id: number, sku_code: string, price: number | null, stock_quantity: number, options: [ { option_name: string, option_value: string } ] } ], avg_rating: number | null, review_count: number, reviews: [ { id: number, customer_id: number, rating: number, content: string | null, created_at: string, is_deleted: boolean } ] }

**POST /sellers/products** (Protected)
- Request Body: { name: string, description: string, category_id: number, base_price: number, images?: [ { image_url: string } ], variants?: [ { sku_code: string, price?: number, options: [ { option_name: string, option_value: string } ] } ] }
- Response: { id: number }
- Authorization: Seller JWT
- Validation: Products must have at least one variant
- Side effect: Creates product snapshot

**PUT /sellers/products/{product_id}** (Protected)
- Request Body: { name?: string, description?: string, category_id?: number, base_price?: number, images?: [ { id?: number, image_url: string, position?: number } ], variants?: [ { id?: number, sku_code?: string, price?: number, options: [ { option_name: string, option_value: string } ] } ] }
- Response: { id: number }
- Authorization: Seller JWT
- Side effect: Creates product snapshot; updates image positions
- Validation: No more than one main image (position=0);
  - If variant options change, must create new variant or update existing by ID

**DELETE /sellers/products/{product_id}** (Protected)
- Response: { success: true }
- Authorization: Seller JWT
- Precondition: No pending order items (paid/shipped), no pending cancellations/refunds

**GET /sellers/products/{product_id}/snapshots** (Protected)
- Query: page?, limit?
- Response: { data: [ { version: number, name: string, description: string, base_price: number, category_id: number, changed_at: string, changed_by: 'seller'|'admin', previous_name: string | null, previous_description: string | null, previous_base_price: number | null, images: [ { image_url: string, position: number } ], variants: [ { sku_code: string, price: number | null, options: [ { option_name: string, option_value: string } ] } ] } ], pagination: { page: number, limit: number, total: number } }
- Authorization: Seller JWT

**GET /admin/products/{product_id}/snapshots**
- Same structure as above
- Authorization: Admin JWT

**GET /admin/products** (Protected)
- Query: page?, limit? 
- Response: [ { id: number, name: string, seller_id: number, category_id: number, base_price: number, created_at: string, is_deleted: boolean, deleted_at: string | null } ]
- Authorization: Admin JWT

**DELETE /admin/products/{product_id}** (Protected)
- Response: { success: true }
- Authorization: Admin JWT

### Product Images

**PUT /sellers/products/{product_id}/images/reorder** (Protected)
- Request Body: [ { id: number, position: number } ]
- Response: { success: true }
- Authorization: Seller JWT
- Side effect: Triggers product snapshot

**DELETE /sellers/products/{product_id}/images/{image_id}** (Protected)
- Response: { success: true }
- Authorization: Seller JWT
- Side effect: Triggers product snapshot

### Product Variants (SKUs)

**POST /sellers/products/{product_id}/variants** (Protected)
- Request Body: { sku_code: string, price?: number, options: [ { option_name: string, option_value: string } ] }
- Response: { id: number }
- Authorization: Seller JWT
- Validation: SKU must be unique across product
- Side effect: Creates variant snapshot

**PUT /sellers/products/{product_id}/variants/{variant_id}** (Protected)
- Request Body: { sku_code?: string, price?: number, options?: [ { option_name: string, option_value: string } ] }
- Response: { id: number }
- Authorization: Seller JWT
- Side effect: Creates variant snapshot
- Validation: SKU must be unique across product

**DELETE /sellers/products/{product_id}/variants/{variant_id}** (Protected)
- Response: { success: true }
- Authorization: Seller JWT
- Precondition: No pending order items (paid/shipped), no pending cancellations/refunds

**GET /sellers/products/{product_id}/variants/{variant_id}/snapshots** (Protected)
- Query: page?, limit?
- Response: { data: [ { version: number, sku_code: string, price: number | null, changed_at: string, changed_by: 'seller'|'admin', previous_sku_code: string | null, previous_price: number | null, options: [ { option_name: string, option_value: string } ] } ], pagination: { page: number, limit: number, total: number } }
- Authorization: Seller JWT

**GET /admin/products/{product_id}/variants/{variant_id}/snapshots**
- Same structure as above
- Authorization: Admin JWT

### Inventory Management

**POST /sellers/inventory/{variant_id}/restock** (Protected)
- Request Body: { quantity: number, reason: 'restock'|'adjustment'|'loss', notes?: string }
- Response: { success: true }
- Authorization: Seller JWT
- Side effect: Creates inventory log record

**POST /sellers/inventory/{variant_id}/adjust** (Protected)
- Request Body: { quantity: number, reason: 'adjustment'|'loss', notes?: string }
- Response: { success: true }
- Authorization: Seller JWT
- Side effect: Creates inventory log record

**GET /sellers/inventory/{variant_id}/history** (Protected)
- Query: page?, limit?
- Response: { data: [ { id: number, change_quantity: number, reason: 'restock'|'order'|'cancellation'|'refund'|'adjustment'|'loss', reference_id: number | null, timestamp: string, notes: string | null } ], pagination: { page: number, limit: number, total: number } }
- Authorization: Seller JWT

### Wishlist

**GET /customers/wishlist** (Protected)
- Query: page?, limit?, sort? ('newest'|'oldest')
- Response: { data: [ { product_id: number, product_name: string, main_image_url: string, seller_shop_name: string, base_price: number, avg_rating: number | null, review_count: number, created_at: string } ], pagination: { page: number, limit: number, total: number } }
- Authorization: Customer JWT

**POST /customers/wishlist** (Protected)
- Request Body: { product_id: number }
- Response: { success: true }
- Authorization: Customer JWT
- Validation: Must not already exist in wishlist

**DELETE /customers/wishlist/{product_id}** (Protected)
- Response: { success: true }
- Authorization: Customer JWT

### Shopping Cart

**GET /customers/cart** (Protected)
- Response: { items: [ { id: number, variant_id: number, product_name: string, sku_code: string, option_values: [ { option_name: string, option_value: string } ], price: number, quantity: number, subtotal: number, in_stock: boolean, image_url: string }, ... ], total_price: number }
- Authorization: Customer JWT

**POST /customers/cart** (Protected)
- Request Body: { variant_id: number, quantity: number (min 1) }
- Response: { id: number, quantity: number }
- Authorization: Customer JWT
- Validation: Only adds if in stock
- Side effect: Combines with existing item if same variant

**PUT /customers/cart/{cart_item_id}** (Protected)
- Request Body: { quantity: number (min 1) }
- Response: { id: number, quantity: number, subtotal: number }
- Authorization: Customer JWT
- Validation: Quantity must be ≤ available stock

**DELETE /customers/cart/{cart_item_id}** (Protected)
- Response: { success: true }
- Authorization: Customer JWT

### Checkout

**POST /customers/checkout** (Protected)
- Request Body: { address_id: number, payment_method?: string }
- Response: { order_id: number, total_price: number, items: [ { id: number, variant_id: number, quantity: number, price_at_time_of_purchase: number } ] }
- Authorization: Customer JWT
- Validation: No unavailable items in cart
- Side effects:
  - Clears cart
  - Creates order record
  - Creates order items with snapshots
  - Updates inventory (decrease stock)

### Order Management

**GET /customers/orders** (Protected)
- Query: page?, limit?, status? ('paid'|'shipped'|'delivered'|'cancelled'|'refunded'|'partially_completed')
- Response: { data: [ { id: number, order_number: string, total_price: number, status: 'paid'|'shipped'|'delivered'|'cancelled'|'refunded'|'partially_completed', created_at: string, shipping_address: { recipient_name: string, street_address: string, city: string, state_province: string, postal_code: string, country: string }, item_count: number } ], pagination: { page: number, limit: number, total: number } }
- Authorization: Customer JWT

**GET /customers/orders/{order_id}** (Protected)
- Response: { id: number, order_number: string, total_price: number, status: 'paid'|'shipped'|'delivered'|'cancelled'|'refunded'|'partially_completed', created_at: string, updated_at: string, shipping_address: { recipient_name: string, street_address: string, city: string, state_province: string, postal_code: string, country: string }, items: [ { id: number, product_name: string, sku_code: string, option_values: [ { option_name: string, option_value: string } ], price_at_time_of_purchase: number, quantity: number, status: 'paid'|'shipped'|'delivered'|'cancelled'|'refunded', seller_shop_name: string, seller_id: number, product_snapshot_id: number, variant_snapshot_id: number, seller_profile_snapshot_id: number } ], shipments: [ { id: number, carrier_name: string, tracking_number: string, shipped_at: string, delivered_at: string | null, items: [ { order_item_id: number } ] } ] }
- Authorization: Customer JWT

**GET /sellers/orders** (Protected)
- Query: status?, page?, limit?
- Response: Same structure as /customers/orders, but filtered by seller's products
- Authorization: Seller JWT

**GET /sellers/orders/{order_id}** (Protected)
- Response: Same as /customers/orders/{order_id}
- Authorization: Seller JWT

**GET /admin/orders** (Protected)
- Query: customer_id?, seller_id?, status?, page?, limit?
- Response: { data: [ ... ], pagination: { ... } }
- Authorization: Admin JWT

**GET /admin/orders/{order_id}** (Protected)
- Response: Same as /customers/orders/{order_id}
- Authorization: Admin JWT

**POST /admin/orders/{order_id}/items/{item_id}/cancel** (Protected)
- Request Body: { reason: string }
- Response: { success: true }
- Authorization: Admin JWT

**POST /admin/orders/{order_id}/items/{item_id}/refund** (Protected)
- Request Body: { reason: string }
- Response: { success: true }
- Authorization: Admin JWT

**POST /admin/orders/{order_id}/cancel** (Protected)
- Request Body: { reason: string }
- Response: { success: true }
- Authorization: Admin JWT

**POST /admin/orders/{order_id}/refund** (Protected)
- Request Body: { reason: string }
- Response: { success: true }
- Authorization: Admin JWT

### Shipment Management

**GET /sellers/order-items/shipment-pending** (Protected)
- Query: page?, limit?
- Response: List of order items with status 'paid' owned by seller, grouped by order
- Authorization: Seller JWT

**POST /sellers/shipments** (Protected)
- Request Body: { order_item_ids: number[], carrier_name: string, tracking_number: string }
- Response: { id: number, carrier_name: string, tracking_number: string, shipped_at: string, items: [ { order_item_id: number } ] }
- Authorization: Seller JWT
- Validation: All items must belong to seller and have status 'paid'
- Side effect: Updates all listed order items to 'shipped'

operations.name: join
operations.description:
Creates a new customer account by validating email uniqueness and storing a cryptographically hashed password. This operation confirms identity through email verification after creation. The registration flow requires the email and password_hash fields from the shopping_mall_customers table. Upon successful join, a session is initiated with access and refresh tokens issued via the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table. This operation is required as the customer actor is a member type with full authentication capability and joins via credential-based registration.

The system MUST validate email uniqueness against the shopping_mall_customers.email field. Passwords are stored as hash in shopping_mall_customers.password_hash and must meet complexity requirements (design implied by schema). Registration creates a new customer record in shopping_mall_customers and an initial session in shopping_mall_customer_sessions. The system must send an email verification token to the provided email, linked to shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications. No pre-authentication state is required; join is the entry point for unauthenticated users.

A successful join response returns an IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized object with a new access token (30-min TTL) and refresh token (30-day TTL), both mapped to the generated session record. Invalid registration (duplicate email, weak password) returns 422. The token generation mechanism relies on the JWT infrastructure supplied by authN service, binding to the customer.id.

This operation has no prerequisites as it is the initial entry point for customer identity creation and does not rely on prior system state. All operations downstream depend on this being completed first. Subsequent operations (login, refresh) require this session state.
operations.specification: The service layer creates a new shopping_mall_customers record with email and password_hash. It generates a unique verification token, inserts it into shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications with 1-hour expiration, and generates a JWT access token (30-min) and refresh token (30-day). These are stored in shopping_mall_customer_sessions with customer_id linked. Session records include IP and referrer for audit. Response returns IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized with tokens. Validation checks: email format, uniqueness in shopping_mall_customers, password length/complexity. Upon failure, no record is created or token generated. Immutable session audit trail maintained.

requestBody.description: Request payload to create a new customer account with email and password.

responseBody.description: Response containing access and refresh JWT tokens and customer identifier post-registration.

operations.name: login
operations.description:
Verifies customer credentials by matching submitted email and password against the stored hash in the shopping_mall_customers table. Upon successful authentication, generates a new JWT access token (30-min) and refresh token (30-day) and stores them in shopping_mall_customer_sessions. This operation is required for all member actors to establish an authenticated session after registration. The customer actor type requires login to access protected resources.

The system validates the email exists in shopping_mall_customers and that the password_hash matches the submitted plaintext password after cryptographic hashing. If both validations pass, it generates new tokens and creates or updates a session record with client IP and referrer context. The operation fails with 401 if credentials mismatch, account is deleted (deleted_at not null), or if server-side technical errors occur.

The defined IShoppingMallCustomer.ILogin body must contain email and password. The IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized response contains the new tokens and the customer ID associated with this login event. The refresh token enables token renewal without re-authenticating credentials.

This operation has no prerequisites as it is the primary entry point for authenticated sessions and does not require prior login or state. It is decoupled from pending email verification — residual verification tokens do not block login if the account exists and credentials are valid.
operations.specification: When login is called, server looks up customer in shopping_mall_customers by email. Checks if deleted_at is null. Computes hash of submitted password and compares to password_hash. On match, generates new JWTs: access token (30m) and refresh token (30d). Inserts new record in shopping_mall_customer_sessions with IP, referrer, and expiry. Returns IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized. On mismatch or account deleted, returns 401. Invalid input (missing email/password) returns 422. All token issuance is stateless and bound by customer_id. No session cleanup occurs on login—previous sessions remain valid unless manually revoked.

requestBody.description: Request containing email and plaintext password to authenticate customer and establish session.

responseBody.description: Response with newly generated access and refresh JWT tokens upon successful authentication.

operations.name: refresh
operations.description:
Renews the access token by validating a previously issued refresh token stored in shopping_mall_customer_sessions. This operation allows the customer to maintain a session without re-entering credentials, reducing exposure to credential harvesting. The refresh token must be valid (not expired, not revoked) and associated with an active customer record. Both tokens persist in the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table for audit and revocation tracking.

The system accepts a refresh token string and validates it against the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table. If the token exists, its expired_at timestamp is later than current time, and the associated customer record has deleted_at = null, then a new access token is generated and returned. The refresh token itself is not renewed unless explicitly designed (per specification, it remains valid until expiration). This operation cements the stateless JWT architecture—no session persistence beyond token validity.

The IShoppingMallCustomer.IRefresh request body expects only the refresh token string. The response IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized returns a new access token with 30-minute TTL. The refresh token remains unchanged. If refresh token is invalid, expired, or belongs to a deleted customer, a 401 Unauthorized is returned.

This operation has no prerequisites. It can be called at any time if a valid refresh token exists, even without prior login during the session. It is the mechanism enabling stateless, long-duration authentication without re-authenticating credentials.
operations.specification: The server looks up the refresh token in shopping_mall_customer_sessions by its value. Checks if expired_at > now and shopping_mall_customers.deleted_at is null for the associated customer_id. If valid, generates new JWT access token (30-min TTL) and returns it in IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized. Refresh token value and expiry remain unchanged. Does NOT update the session entry—session expiration is unchanged. Returns 401 if token not found, expired, or linked to deleted user. No side effects on database other than token issuance. Access token issued without verifying user password. Only token trust is needed.

requestBody.description: Request body containing a valid refresh token to renew access token without re-authentication.

responseBody.description: Response containing only a new access token, with unchanged refresh token.

operations.specification: The join operation accepts a seller's email and password as input, validates that the email is unique and the password meets complexity requirements (min 12 chars, mixed case, special symbol, no common patterns), then creates a new shopping_mall_sellers record with is_active = true, status = 'pending', and password_hash as a bcrypt hash of the input password. The operation returns a 201 status with IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized containing a 30-minute access token and 30-day refresh token. No session is created yet—session creation occurs on first login after email verification. Email verification token is created separately by a service layer after this operation.
operations.description:
Sellers register on the platform by submitting their email address and password to create an account. This operation validates that the email is not already registered and that the password meets minimum security requirements (minimum 12 characters, including uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special symbols). Upon validation, a new record is created in the shopping_mall_sellers table, where the email and bcrypt-hashed password are stored. The seller's initial status is set to 'pending' to indicate the account is awaiting admin approval. The operation does not create a session—authentication is not yet complete, and login is blocked until the seller's registration is approved by an administrator. After successful registration, an email verification record is automatically created in shopping_mall_seller_email_verifications for the seller, which is used for separate email confirmation, not for authentication purposes. The response body returns an IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized object containing the newly generated 30-minute access token and 30-day refresh token, allowing the seller to maintain their registration state on the client side, regardless of admin approval status. This implementation ensures that registration and authentication are decoupled—a seller must be registered before they can authenticate, but registration only initiates the onboarding flow.

Security considerations: The password_hash field is never returned in any response, and only bcrypt-hashed values are stored in the database, never plaintext. The operation enforces password complexity rules client-side and server-side to prevent weak passwords. A rate limit of 5 attempts per IP per hour applies to prevent brute-force registration attacks. The operation does not perform email verification during registration—this is handled as a separate workflow via the emailed verification link.

Related operations: This is the first step in the seller authentication lifecycle, followed by login after approval. Admins use the /admin/sellers/pending-approvals endpoint to approve or reject registrations. No refresh or logout operation is required during registration. The IShoppingMallSeller.IJoin request body schema enforces strict typing for email and password to ensure schema compliance.

The system does not store any personal identifiers beyond email and password_hash at this stage; profile data (shop name, logo, etc.) is only added after approval via the PUT /sellers/me endpoint, which triggers a seller profile snapshot. This separation ensures that authentication identity and business identity are distinct, aligning with the snapshot principle for transactional integrity.

requestBody.description: Request body containing email and password for new seller registration.

responseBody.description: Response containing the access token and refresh token issued upon successful registration. The seller is not yet approved for login; this token exists for session state, not authentication authority.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: The login operation validates a seller's email and password against the shopping_mall_sellers table. It checks that the account is active (is_active = true), not deleted (deleted_at is null), and approved (status = 'approved'). If valid, it generates a 30-minute access token and a 30-day refresh token, and creates a corresponding session record in shopping_mall_seller_sessions with the client's IP and referrer. The operation returns an IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized token object. If the seller is pending or rejected, a 403 error is returned. Suspended accounts (suspended_at not null) are treated as inactive and return 403.
operations.description:
Sellers authenticate their identity by providing their email and password to obtain a valid access and refresh token. This operation validates the seller's credentials against the shopping_mall_sellers table, ensuring the email exists, the password hash matches, and the account has been approved by an administrator (status = 'approved'). The account must be active (is_active = true) and not marked as deleted (deleted_at IS NULL) or temporarily suspended (suspended_at IS NULL). Upon successful authentication, the system generates a 30-minute access token and a 30-day refresh token, both JWT-encoded with RS256 signing. A corresponding session record is created in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table, capturing the client's IP address, referrer URL, and creation timestamp, enabling security auditing and device tracking. The response body returns an IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized object containing the two tokens. If the seller's registration status is 'pending' or 'rejected', or if the account is suspended or deleted, a 403 Forbidden error is returned, preventing login. This ensures that only approved sellers can access the API endpoints.

Security considerations: Passwords are never transmitted or stored in plaintext—bcrypt hashing is used for storage and comparison. The operation enforces rate limiting at 10 failed attempts per IP per 10 minutes to prevent brute-force attacks. All tokens are signed and encrypted and include claims for issuer, audience, expiration, subject (seller_id), and issued-at time. The refresh token can be revoked by deleting the session record in shopping_mall_seller_sessions or by setting a seller's suspended_at or deleted_at field, which invalidates all active sessions.

Related operations: After login, sellers may use the refresh token to renew their access token without re-entering credentials. This operation has no prerequisite other than correct credentials and approved status. It does not trigger profile data modification or session cleanup—those are handled by separate endpoints. The IShoppingMallSeller.ILogin request body schema strictly requires email and password fields to enforce schema compliance.

The platform follows the principle of separation of concerns: registration creates a pending account, login activates the account if approved, and refresh maintains the session without re-authentication. Logout is not implemented, as token revocation is handled server-side by session invalidation.

requestBody.description: Request body containing email and password for seller authentication.

responseBody.description: Response containing the access token and refresh token issued upon successful authentication. Contains the seller's ID and authentication status.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: The refresh operation validates a seller's refresh token against the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table. It checks that the token has not expired and the associated session is still active (deleted_at IS NULL). If valid, it generates a new 30-minute access token and a new 30-day refresh token, updates the session record with the new refresh token, and returns the updated IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized object. The old refresh token is rendered invalid immediately upon use.
operations.description:
Sellers refresh their access token without re-entering their credentials by submitting a valid refresh token. This operation verifies that the refresh token is valid and has not expired, and that the corresponding session in shopping_mall_seller_sessions is active (deleted_at IS NULL). If validation passes, the system generates a new 30-minute access token and a new 30-day refresh token, and updates the session record with the new refresh token value, automatically rendering the old refresh token invalid to prevent replay attacks. The operation returns an IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized response object with the new tokens. Refresh tokens are single-use and are automatically invalidated after one use or if the seller logs in from another device. This ensures token security and prevents session hijacking.

Security considerations: The refresh token is only accepted if it matches a current and active session. Token rotation (immediate invalidation of old token) is mandatory. The operation checks the client's IP address and user-agent against the session record to detect anomalies. If there is a mismatch, a security alert is logged and the refresh request is rejected. The refresh endpoint is rate-limited to 2 requests per hour per seller to prevent abuse. The operation does not trigger authentication events or profile updates—it is purely a token maintenance mechanism.

Related operations: This operation assumes a valid login has already occurred. It cannot be used if the session was deleted (e.g., after an admin suspends the seller). It does not require any authentication actor since it operates solely on the refresh token. The IShoppingMallSeller.IRefresh request body schema requires only the refresh_token field for compliance.

The platform follows the zero-trust principle: every access token is short-lived, and every refresh requires explicit validation of the session state. Logout is not implemented, as session invalidation is handled by revoking the refresh token via admin action or deletion of the session record.

requestBody.description: Request body containing the refresh token to renew the access token.

responseBody.description: Response containing newly issued access and refresh tokens upon successful refresh. Includes updated session metadata.

The email must not already be registered in the shopping_mall_admins table. The operation does not require email verification to proceed — pending verification status is managed internally via the shopping_mall_admin_email_verifications table, which triggers a separate email confirmation workflow after the join completion. This ensures that the authentication flow is not blocked by external validation, in accordance with the platform's principle of immediate system access upon identity creation. The request body type IShoppingMallAdmin.IJoin defines the structure: { email: string, password: string }, ensuring type safety and schema compliance. This operation is the foundational entry point for any new administrator to gain access to the administrative interface.

operations.name: refresh

If the refresh token is valid, not expired, and not blacklisted, the system issues a new access token (30 min expiry) and a new refresh token (30 day expiry), replacing the old one. The old refresh token is invalidated and removed from the session store. The new refresh token is stored, and the expiration is reset. This operation supports seamless long-term session persistence without requiring the admin to re-enter credentials. It does not validate email or password — only token validity and integrity. The request body type IShoppingMallAdmin.IRefresh defines the structure: { refresh_token: string }, ensuring only the token is exchanged. This mechanism prevents token theft since even if an access token is intercepted, it cannot renew itself without the refresh token.

operations.specification: The system validates the refresh token by looking it up in shopping_mall_admin_sessions. The admin_id is derived from the session record. All operations use strict atomic database transactions to prevent race conditions.
