The system MUST validate email uniqueness against the shopping_mall_customers.email field. Passwords are stored as hash in shopping_mall_customers.password_hash and must meet complexity requirements (design implied by schema). Registration creates a new customer record in shopping_mall_customers and an initial session in shopping_mall_customer_sessions. The system must send an email verification token to the provided email, linked to shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications. No pre-authentication state is required; join is the entry point for unauthenticated users.

A successful join response returns an IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized object with a new access token (30-min TTL) and refresh token (30-day TTL), both mapped to the generated session record. Invalid registration (duplicate email, weak password) returns 422. The token generation mechanism relies on the JWT infrastructure supplied by authN service, binding to the customer.id.

This operation has no prerequisites as it is the initial entry point for customer identity creation and does not rely on prior system state. All operations downstream depend on this being completed first. Subsequent operations (login, refresh) require this session state.
operations.specification: The service layer creates a new shopping_mall_customers record with email and password_hash. It generates a unique verification token, inserts it into shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications with 1-hour expiration, and generates a JWT access token (30-min) and refresh token (30-day). These are stored in shopping_mall_customer_sessions with customer_id linked. Session records include IP and referrer for audit. Response returns IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized with tokens. Validation checks: email format, uniqueness in shopping_mall_customers, password length/complexity. Upon failure, no record is created or token generated. Immutable session audit trail maintained.

requestBody.description: Request payload to create a new customer account with email and password.

responseBody.description: Response containing access and refresh JWT tokens and customer identifier post-registration.

operations.name: login
operations.description:
Verifies customer credentials by matching submitted email and password against the stored hash in the shopping_mall_customers table. Upon successful authentication, generates a new JWT access token (30-min) and refresh token (30-day) and stores them in shopping_mall_customer_sessions. This operation is required for all member actors to establish an authenticated session after registration. The customer actor type requires login to access protected resources.

The system validates the email exists in shopping_mall_customers and that the password_hash matches the submitted plaintext password after cryptographic hashing. If both validations pass, it generates new tokens and creates or updates a session record with client IP and referrer context. The operation fails with 401 if credentials mismatch, account is deleted (deleted_at not null), or if server-side technical errors occur.

The defined IShoppingMallCustomer.ILogin body must contain email and password. The IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized response contains the new tokens and the customer ID associated with this login event. The refresh token enables token renewal without re-authenticating credentials.

This operation has no prerequisites as it is the primary entry point for authenticated sessions and does not require prior login or state. It is decoupled from pending email verification — residual verification tokens do not block login if the account exists and credentials are valid.
operations.specification: When login is called, server looks up customer in shopping_mall_customers by email. Checks if deleted_at is null. Computes hash of submitted password and compares to password_hash. On match, generates new JWTs: access token (30m) and refresh token (30d). Inserts new record in shopping_mall_customer_sessions with IP, referrer, and expiry. Returns IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized. On mismatch or account deleted, returns 401. Invalid input (missing email/password) returns 422. All token issuance is stateless and bound by customer_id. No session cleanup occurs on login—previous sessions remain valid unless manually revoked.

requestBody.description: Request containing email and plaintext password to authenticate customer and establish session.

responseBody.description: Response with newly generated access and refresh JWT tokens upon successful authentication.

operations.name: refresh
operations.description:
Renews the access token by validating a previously issued refresh token stored in shopping_mall_customer_sessions. This operation allows the customer to maintain a session without re-entering credentials, reducing exposure to credential harvesting. The refresh token must be valid (not expired, not revoked) and associated with an active customer record. Both tokens persist in the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table for audit and revocation tracking.

The system accepts a refresh token string and validates it against the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table. If the token exists, its expired_at timestamp is later than current time, and the associated customer record has deleted_at = null, then a new access token is generated and returned. The refresh token itself is not renewed unless explicitly designed (per specification, it remains valid until expiration). This operation cements the stateless JWT architecture—no session persistence beyond token validity.

The IShoppingMallCustomer.IRefresh request body expects only the refresh token string. The response IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized returns a new access token with 30-minute TTL. The refresh token remains unchanged. If refresh token is invalid, expired, or belongs to a deleted customer, a 401 Unauthorized is returned.

This operation has no prerequisites. It can be called at any time if a valid refresh token exists, even without prior login during the session. It is the mechanism enabling stateless, long-duration authentication without re-authenticating credentials.
operations.specification: The server looks up the refresh token in shopping_mall_customer_sessions by its value. Checks if expired_at > now and shopping_mall_customers.deleted_at is null for the associated customer_id. If valid, generates new JWT access token (30-min TTL) and returns it in IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized. Refresh token value and expiry remain unchanged. Does NOT update the session entry—session expiration is unchanged. Returns 401 if token not found, expired, or linked to deleted user. No side effects on database other than token issuance. Access token issued without verifying user password. Only token trust is needed.

requestBody.description: Request body containing a valid refresh token to renew access token without re-authentication.

responseBody.description: Response containing only a new access token, with unchanged refresh token.

operations.specification: The join operation accepts a seller's email and password as input, validates that the email is unique and the password meets complexity requirements (min 12 chars, mixed case, special symbol, no common patterns), then creates a new shopping_mall_sellers record with is_active = true, status = 'pending', and password_hash as a bcrypt hash of the input password. The operation returns a 201 status with IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized containing a 30-minute access token and 30-day refresh token. No session is created yet—session creation occurs on first login after email verification. Email verification token is created separately by a service layer after this operation.
operations.description:
Sellers register on the platform by submitting their email address and password to create an account. This operation validates that the email is not already registered and that the password meets minimum security requirements (minimum 12 characters, including uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special symbols). Upon validation, a new record is created in the shopping_mall_sellers table, where the email and bcrypt-hashed password are stored. The seller's initial status is set to 'pending' to indicate the account is awaiting admin approval. The operation does not create a session—authentication is not yet complete, and login is blocked until the seller's registration is approved by an administrator. After successful registration, an email verification record is automatically created in shopping_mall_seller_email_verifications for the seller, which is used for separate email confirmation, not for authentication purposes. The response body returns an IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized object containing the newly generated 30-minute access token and 30-day refresh token, allowing the seller to maintain their registration state on the client side, regardless of admin approval status. This implementation ensures that registration and authentication are decoupled—a seller must be registered before they can authenticate, but registration only initiates the onboarding flow.

Security considerations: The password_hash field is never returned in any response, and only bcrypt-hashed values are stored in the database, never plaintext. The operation enforces password complexity rules client-side and server-side to prevent weak passwords. A rate limit of 5 attempts per IP per hour applies to prevent brute-force registration attacks. The operation does not perform email verification during registration—this is handled as a separate workflow via the emailed verification link.

Related operations: This is the first step in the seller authentication lifecycle, followed by login after approval. Admins use the /admin/sellers/pending-approvals endpoint to approve or reject registrations. No refresh or logout operation is required during registration. The IShoppingMallSeller.IJoin request body schema enforces strict typing for email and password to ensure schema compliance.

The system does not store any personal identifiers beyond email and password_hash at this stage; profile data (shop name, logo, etc.) is only added after approval via the PUT /sellers/me endpoint, which triggers a seller profile snapshot. This separation ensures that authentication identity and business identity are distinct, aligning with the snapshot principle for transactional integrity.

requestBody.description: Request body containing email and password for new seller registration.

responseBody.description: Response containing the access token and refresh token issued upon successful registration. The seller is not yet approved for login; this token exists for session state, not authentication authority.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: The login operation validates a seller's email and password against the shopping_mall_sellers table. It checks that the account is active (is_active = true), not deleted (deleted_at is null), and approved (status = 'approved'). If valid, it generates a 30-minute access token and a 30-day refresh token, and creates a corresponding session record in shopping_mall_seller_sessions with the client's IP and referrer. The operation returns an IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized token object. If the seller is pending or rejected, a 403 error is returned. Suspended accounts (suspended_at not null) are treated as inactive and return 403.
operations.description:
Sellers authenticate their identity by providing their email and password to obtain a valid access and refresh token. This operation validates the seller's credentials against the shopping_mall_sellers table, ensuring the email exists, the password hash matches, and the account has been approved by an administrator (status = 'approved'). The account must be active (is_active = true) and not marked as deleted (deleted_at IS NULL) or temporarily suspended (suspended_at IS NULL). Upon successful authentication, the system generates a 30-minute access token and a 30-day refresh token, both JWT-encoded with RS256 signing. A corresponding session record is created in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table, capturing the client's IP address, referrer URL, and creation timestamp, enabling security auditing and device tracking. The response body returns an IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized object containing the two tokens. If the seller's registration status is 'pending' or 'rejected', or if the account is suspended or deleted, a 403 Forbidden error is returned, preventing login. This ensures that only approved sellers can access the API endpoints.

Security considerations: Passwords are never transmitted or stored in plaintext—bcrypt hashing is used for storage and comparison. The operation enforces rate limiting at 10 failed attempts per IP per 10 minutes to prevent brute-force attacks. All tokens are signed and encrypted and include claims for issuer, audience, expiration, subject (seller_id), and issued-at time. The refresh token can be revoked by deleting the session record in shopping_mall_seller_sessions or by setting a seller's suspended_at or deleted_at field, which invalidates all active sessions.

Related operations: After login, sellers may use the refresh token to renew their access token without re-entering credentials. This operation has no prerequisite other than correct credentials and approved status. It does not trigger profile data modification or session cleanup—those are handled by separate endpoints. The IShoppingMallSeller.ILogin request body schema strictly requires email and password fields to enforce schema compliance.

The platform follows the principle of separation of concerns: registration creates a pending account, login activates the account if approved, and refresh maintains the session without re-authentication. Logout is not implemented, as token revocation is handled server-side by session invalidation.

requestBody.description: Request body containing email and password for seller authentication.

responseBody.description: Response containing the access token and refresh token issued upon successful authentication. Contains the seller's ID and authentication status.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: The refresh operation validates a seller's refresh token against the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table. It checks that the token has not expired and the associated session is still active (deleted_at IS NULL). If valid, it generates a new 30-minute access token and a new 30-day refresh token, updates the session record with the new refresh token, and returns the updated IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized object. The old refresh token is rendered invalid immediately upon use.
operations.description:
Sellers refresh their access token without re-entering their credentials by submitting a valid refresh token. This operation verifies that the refresh token is valid and has not expired, and that the corresponding session in shopping_mall_seller_sessions is active (deleted_at IS NULL). If validation passes, the system generates a new 30-minute access token and a new 30-day refresh token, and updates the session record with the new refresh token value, automatically rendering the old refresh token invalid to prevent replay attacks. The operation returns an IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized response object with the new tokens. Refresh tokens are single-use and are automatically invalidated after one use or if the seller logs in from another device. This ensures token security and prevents session hijacking.

Security considerations: The refresh token is only accepted if it matches a current and active session. Token rotation (immediate invalidation of old token) is mandatory. The operation checks the client's IP address and user-agent against the session record to detect anomalies. If there is a mismatch, a security alert is logged and the refresh request is rejected. The refresh endpoint is rate-limited to 2 requests per hour per seller to prevent abuse. The operation does not trigger authentication events or profile updates—it is purely a token maintenance mechanism.

Related operations: This operation assumes a valid login has already occurred. It cannot be used if the session was deleted (e.g., after an admin suspends the seller). It does not require any authentication actor since it operates solely on the refresh token. The IShoppingMallSeller.IRefresh request body schema requires only the refresh_token field for compliance.

The platform follows the zero-trust principle: every access token is short-lived, and every refresh requires explicit validation of the session state. Logout is not implemented, as session invalidation is handled by revoking the refresh token via admin action or deletion of the session record.

requestBody.description: Request body containing the refresh token to renew the access token.

responseBody.description: Response containing newly issued access and refresh tokens upon successful refresh. Includes updated session metadata.

operations.name: refresh
join
operations.description: Registers a new system administrator account. This operation requires the admin to provide a valid email address and password. The email must not already be registered in the shopping_mall_admins table. Upon successful registration, the system creates a new admin record with password hashing and issues an initial JWT access and refresh token. The operation does not require email verification to proceed — pending verification status is managed internally via the shopping_mall_admin_email_verifications table, which triggers a separate email confirmation workflow after the join completion. This ensures that the authentication flow is not blocked by external validation, in accordance with the platform's principle of immediate system access upon identity creation. The request body type IShoppingMallAdmin.IJoin defines the structure: { email: string, password: string }, ensuring type safety and schema compliance. This operation is the foundational entry point for any new administrator to gain access to the administrative interface.

requestBody.description: Request body for creating a new admin account with email and password. Must include a valid email (non-empty, valid format) and a password meeting security requirements (minimum 8 characters). No other fields are permitted.

responseBody.description: Response body for admin join operation returning JWT access and refresh tokens. Contains access_token, refresh_token, and admin_id fields for session persistence and authorization.

operations.specification: The service layer creates a new record in shopping_mall_admins with hashed password. It generates a JWT access token (30 min expiry) and refresh token (30 day expiry). The refresh token is stored in shopping_mall_admin_sessions. It does not trigger or wait for email verification — that is handled asynchronously via a separate system event. Returns success with tokens on success. If email exists, returns 409 Conflict. If password is too weak, returns 422 Unprocessable Entity. All responses are typed and validated by the Prisma schema and NestJS DTO validation.

operations.name: login
operations.description: Authenticates a registered administrator and issues access and refresh JWT tokens. The system validates the provided email and password against the shopping_mall_admins table. The email must be registered and the password must hash-match the stored value. The operation is rejected if the admin account is suspended or has been permanently banned. Upon successful authentication, an access token with 30-minute expiration and a refresh token with 30-day expiration are returned. The refresh token is stored in the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table to support token refresh cycles. This operation does not verify email status — a suspended account returns 403 Forbidden without disclosing whether the issue is suspension, deletion, or wrong credentials, enhancing security. The response includes admin_id to identify the authenticated actor. The request body type IShoppingMallAdmin.ILogin defines the structure: { email: string, password: string }, ensuring strict type compliance.

requestBody.description: Request body for logging in an admin account. Must contain a valid email and password. No other fields are allowed. Password is transmitted securely as plaintext over HTTPS and is never stored; hashing occurs server-side.

responseBody.description: Response body for admin login operation returning JWT access and refresh tokens. Contains access_token, refresh_token, and admin_id fields for session persistence and authorization.

operations.specification: The system retrieves the admin record from shopping_mall_admins using the email. Verifies the password using bcrypt comparison. If account is suspended (suspended_at not null), returns 403 Forbidden. If authentication fails, returns 401 Unauthorized. Upon success, generates tokens and stores refresh token in shopping_mall_admin_sessions. Returns tokens with admin_id. All logic is transactional and secured with rate limiting on auth attempts per email.

operations.name: refresh
operations.description: Renews a valid access token using a valid refresh token. The operation requires the client to submit a previously issued refresh token from the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table. If the refresh token is valid, not expired, and not blacklisted, the system issues a new access token (30 min expiry) and a new refresh token (30 day expiry), replacing the old one. The old refresh token is invalidated and removed from the session store. The new refresh token is stored, and the expiration is reset. This operation supports seamless long-term session persistence without requiring the admin to re-enter credentials. It does not validate email or password — only token validity and integrity. The request body type IShoppingMallAdmin.IRefresh defines the structure: { refresh_token: string }, ensuring only the token is exchanged. This mechanism prevents token theft since even if an access token is intercepted, it cannot renew itself without the refresh token.

requestBody.description: Request body for refreshing admin tokens. Must contain one field: refresh_token, which is a valid refresh token previously issued by the system and still active within its 30-day window.

responseBody.description: Response body for admin refresh operation returning new JWT access and refresh tokens. Contains access_token, refresh_token, and admin_id fields for session persistence and authorization.

operations.specification: The system validates the refresh token by looking it up in shopping_mall_admin_sessions. If found and not expired, it generates new access and refresh tokens, deletes the old refresh token entry, and inserts the new one. If token is invalid, expired, or missing, returns 401 Unauthorized. The admin_id is derived from the session record. All operations use strict atomic database transactions to prevent race conditions.

Retrieve authenticated customer profile. Requires valid JWT token. Returns display_name, phone_number, and default_address_id from shopping_mall_customers table. No joins required. Return null for optional fields if not set. Apply authorization check before response.
operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated customer's profile information.

This endpoint returns the personal profile details of the currently authenticated customer, including their display name, phone number, and default shipping address ID. All fields are optional and may return null if not set by the customer.

Access to this endpoint requires a valid JWT authentication token issued during customer login. The system does not expose email addresses or password hashes through this API. Profile data is updated only when explicitly modified by the customer through the PUT /customers/me endpoint.

Important: This endpoint is specific to customer accounts. Seller profile information is accessible via a separate endpoint at /sellers/me. The system enforces complete separation of customer and seller identity data to maintain audit trail integrity and prevent confusion between actor types.

When a customer account is deleted, this endpoint will return a 404 Not Found error. Previously created order histories and reviews remain accessible separately.

responseBody.description: Customer profile data including display name, phone number, and default address reference.

operations.name: at

operations.description:
Update the customer's profile information including display name and phone number.

This endpoint allows a registered customer to modify their display name and/or phone number. The operation is subject to strict validation: display_name must comply with alphanumeric and space-hyphen-underscore rules (max 50 characters), and phone_number must be in E.164 international format. If either field is provided as null or empty, it will be set to null in the database. The existing account email and password remain unchanged. This update does not create a snapshot because customer profile fields are not part of the immutable snapshot principle per 02-user-actors.md.

The operation is protected by customer JWT authentication. After successful update, the entire profile object is returned with the updated values. Attempts to update fields not permitted (e.g., email, created_at) will be rejected with 422 error.

Related operations:
- GET /customers/me: Retrieve current profile details
- PUT /sellers/me: Update seller profile (separate endpoint)
- POST /auth/customers/signup: Create a new customer account

When a customer deletes their account, all profile data is removed, but this endpoint is inaccessible during account deletion.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Fetch customer record by authenticated ID. Validate display_name against pattern^[a-zA-Z0-9 _-]+$ and length≤50. Validate phone_number against E.164 format. If display_name is null or empty string, set to null. If phone_number is null or empty string, set to null. Update updated_at timestamp to current UTC. Use atomic transaction to ensure data integrity. Return full customer object with updated fields. Reject if customer is deleted (deleted_at is not null).

requestBody.description: Updateable customer profile fields. Only display_name and phone_number can be modified.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of active user sessions across all actor types.

This endpoint enables administrators and system services to audit and manage active authentication sessions across the platform. Sessions may belong to customers, sellers, or administrators, and can be filtered by actor type, token status, expiration date, and issuance time.

Each session represents an active JWT authentication state with associated access and refresh tokens. Valid sessions are authenticated and active; expired sessions have their access token time window passed; invalidated sessions have been explicitly logged out or flagged for security reasons.

This operation should be used in conjunction with user management and security monitoring tools. The response includes summary information optimized for session management dashboards, with details available through the underlying user and authentication records.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_customer_sessions, shopping_mall_seller_sessions, and shopping_mall_admin_sessions tables.
Filter by actor_type (customer, seller, admin), status (active, expired, invalidated), token_issued_at range, and token_expires_at range.
Join with respective user tables (shopping_mall_customers, shopping_mall_sellers, shopping_mall_admins) to get user email or display name.
Apply pagination with cursor-based offset to support large datasets.
Return only the most recent session per actor session_id to avoid duplicates.
Order results by token_issued_at DESC to show most recent sessions first.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of session summary records

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering active sessions

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed metadata for a specific active session by session ID.

This endpoint allows authenticated customers and administrators to view the context of their own active authentication sessions. The response includes IP address, referring page, and timestamps to support security monitoring and session audit.

Sessions are created upon successful login and remain active until expiration. Access to this endpoint is restricted to the owner of the session. Only sessions belonging to the authenticated user may be retrieved. System does not expose session metadata for other users.

Session expiration is enforced automatically. Expired sessions are not returned. The expired_at timestamp indicates when the access token will expire (30 minutes) and when the refresh token will expire (30 days).

Use this endpoint to diagnose login inconsistencies or detect unauthorized access.

Related operations: POST /auth/customers/login, POST /auth/sellers/login, DELETE /auth/customers/account, DELETE /auth/sellers/account.

Validate that the authenticated user (via JWT token) owns this session by comparing shopping_mall_customer_id to the authenticated user ID. Return all fields: ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at. Return 404 if session not found. Return 403 if session does not belong to authenticated user. No caching.

Retrieve detailed profile information for a specific customer account.

This endpoint returns immutable customer profile data including display name, phone number, and account creation/update timestamps. The response provides sufficient information for customer-facing UI components while preserving privacy by excluding sensitive data like email and password_hash.

Authorized only for administrators as defined in 02-user-actors.md under "View all users" permission. Customers may NOT access other customers' profiles using this endpoint. This is an admin-only operation for support and oversight purposes.

Profile data is not subject to modification via this endpoint. To update customer information, use the PUT /customers/me endpoint instead.

Return 404 if customer not found or if deleted_at is not null. Return 403 if requester is not the same customer and not an admin.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of all user accounts on the shopping_mall platform.

This operation provides administrative access to a comprehensive view of all user accounts — including customers, sellers, and administrators — enabling platform oversight, user management, and moderation. Admins can filter users by status (active, suspended, deleted), role (customer, seller, admin), and perform partial name/email matching searches. Each returned user is represented by a summary view optimized for list display, with minimal sensitive data exposed.

The response includes paginated data with totalCount, currentPage, and perPage metadata, supporting efficient navigation across large user sets. Search is case-insensitive and matches against email or display_name (for customers) or shop_name (for sellers). Filtering is performed server-side and respects the user_type discriminator and soft delete state (deleted_at null = active).

This operation supports bulk user management workflows, such as suspending inactive accounts, approving pending sellers, or auditing administrative access. All results are ordered by created_at descending to prioritize recent registrations. This endpoint requires Admin-level authorization and logs all access for audit purposes.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_users table with JOIN to related customer/seller/admin tables if needed for display_name/shop_name. Apply filters on status (active/suspended/deleted), user_type (customer/seller/admin), and search against email or associated display_name/shop_name fields. Use offset-based pagination with limit and page parameters from request body. Return only is_active=true and deleted_at=null records unless explicitly filtering for deleted accounts. Exclude password_hash and other sensitive fields from response. Log every access for audit trail.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of user summary records for administrative display.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for user list.

operations.description:
Update an existing product's details, images, and variants. This operation allows sellers to modify the product name, description, category, base price, associated images, and product variants.

The system automatically creates a new product snapshot in shopping_mall_product_snapshots with the previous state before applying changes. All variant modifications trigger corresponding shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots records. Images are updated based on position changes, and deletions are handled by marking deleted_at. Category ID must reference an existing, non-deleted category. Current product state is validated against seller ownership and active status.

If any variant's stock quantity is updated, inventory_logs are automatically generated to track modifications. The operation fails if the product has existing 'paid' or 'shipped' order items during variant deletion or if the seller has exceeded their product limit (1,000 active products). All updates must be atomic—for any failed sub-operation, the entire request is rolled back.

This operation depends on GET /products/{product_id} to validate current product state before update. Product snapshots can be reviewed using GET /sellers/products/{product_id}/snapshots.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update product state atomically using transaction. 
1. Validate seller owns product and product is active (deleted_at is null)
2. Validate target category exists and is not deleted
3. Check seller has not exceeded 1,000 active products limit before update
4. For each image in request:
   - If image has id: update position and mark deleted_at if missing from request
   - If image has url but no id: create new image record
5. For each variant in request:
   - If variant has id: update sku_code, price, options and create variant snapshot
   - If variant has no id: create new variant with snapshot
   - If variant id not in request: check if it has order items in 'paid' or 'shipped' status; if yes, reject deletion
6. Apply updated name, description, category_id, base_price to product
7. Generate product snapshot with current state
8. Return updated product object with all fields
9. On any failure, rollback entire transaction and return appropriate error

responseBody.description: The updated product with all current fields, including images and variants. Represents the final state after applying all changes and snapshot creation.

parameters.description: The unique UUID identifier of the product to update. Must belong to the authenticated seller.
parameters.name: productId

requestBody.description: Update request containing new values for product name, description, category, base price, associated images, and variants. All fields are optional. Only provided fields are updated. Variant updates must include either id or sku_code to match existing.

operations.description:
Permanently delete a product from the catalog after verifying no dependent order items, cancellations, or refunds exist. This operation is irreversible and complies with the snapshot principle by preserving all historical product state in shopping_mall_product_snapshots.

This endpoint enforces strict validation to prevent data integrity violations: deletion is prohibited if any variant of the product has order items with status 'paid' or 'shipped', or if there are any pending cancellation or refund requests related to its variants. This ensures all financial transactions linked to the product remain traceable and unaltered.

The deletion process follows the snapshot principle: even though the product is removed from active listings and search results, all variant states, pricing details, and seller profile associations at the time of creation and modification are preserved in immutable snapshots. This allows historical order records to remain accurate and resolvable for dispute resolution.

The product identifier (UUID) remains referenceable in all order item snapshots even after deletion, enabling customer and administrator views of past purchases to display preserved product names, descriptions, and images exactly as they appeared during purchase. Any attempt to modify or delete product snapshots is strictly prohibited.

The operation is only accessible to the product's owning seller or a system administrator. Seller-initiated deletion triggers administrative notification. Admin-initiated deletion archives the product for legal compliance purposes and logs all actions with operator and timestamp for audit trails.

This operation is directly related to: POST /sellers/products (product creation), POST /sellers/products/{product_id}/variants (variant creation), and GET /sellers/products/{product_id}/snapshots (viewing historical state). After successful deletion, these operations become inaccessible for this product.

operations.specification:
Retrieve product record by productId.
Check all variants of the product.
For each variant:
- Count order items with status 'paid' or 'shipped'
- Check pending cancellation requests
- Check pending refund requests
If any record exists:
  - Return 409 Conflict with detailed message listing affected variants
Else:
  - Update product.deleted_at with current timestamp (logical delete)
  - Set product.is_active to false
  - Remove product from search index
  - Delete all associated images (logical)
  - Preserve all product snapshots as immutable records
  - Log deletion with actor and timestamp
  - Return 204 No Content

Cancellation requests for order items must be resolved before product deletion to preserve financial transaction integrity.
Refund requests for delivered order items must be resolved before product deletion to ensure accurate financial reconciliation and historical record.

operations.specification: Validate that the requesting actor is a seller with ownership of the product. Validate that the product exists and is not deleted. Validate that the product has fewer than 10 existing images. Validate that the image_url is a valid, non-empty string. Assign the next position value (max existing position + 1). Create a new shopping_mall_product_images record with: product_id, image_url, position, created_at, and deleted_at = null. Insert into database within transaction. Trigger automatic creation of a product snapshot (shopping_mall_product_snapshots) with the updated image array. Return the full created record including generated id, position, and timestamps.
operations.description:
Upload a new image to a product's gallery.

This endpoint allows authorized sellers to add new product images to their product listings. Each image is stored in immutable object storage and associated with a specific product through a dedicated database record. The system maintains the display order via a position index, and the first image in the order serves as the product thumbnail.

The upload process is atomic and triggers an automatic product snapshot to preserve the product's visual state at the time of modification, supporting historical accuracy for reviews, orders, and audits. The request body must contain a valid HTTPS URL to an image file previously uploaded to object storage.

Images are validated for maximum quantity (10 per product). No file type validation is enforced at the API level as the URL must already reference a valid file. The system does not generate thumbnails server-side; clients must handle image optimization.

This operation cannot be used to reorder or delete existing images. Use dedicated endpoints for those actions.

Related operations:
- PUT /products/{productId}/images/reorder: reorders existing images
- DELETE /products/{productId}/images/{imageId}: removes an image
- GET /products/{productId}/images: lists all images for a product
- GET /products/{productId}/snapshots: views historical image state

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product to which the image will be attached. Must be a valid UUID of an active product owned by the authenticated seller.

requestBody.description: The URL of the uploaded image file to associate with this product.

responseBody.description: The complete record of the newly created product image including its ID, position, and metadata.

Update all image position values atomically using a single transaction. Set the image with position 0 as the primary thumbnail. Create a product snapshot with the previous and new image order. Return success if all validations pass. Do not update images that belong to a different product or have invalid positions.
operations.description:
Reorder the images associated with a product to control display sequence and thumbnail selection.

This operation allows sellers to define the visual order of product images, which directly impacts customer experience and the primary thumbnail displayed in listings. The first image in the updated sequence becomes the main product image.

All changes are preserved as an immutable product snapshot to ensure historical accuracy in case of disputes or audits. This operation is restricted to the product's seller and requires explicit authorization. Images cannot be reordered across products or during product deletion states. The system enforces a maximum of 10 images per product with positions strictly between 0 and 9.

The operation triggers an audit trail in the product snapshot system, ensuring that the exact visual presentation of the product at any point in time can be reconstructed. This is critical for resolving customer disputes where product imagery is a point of contention.

parameters.name: productId

responseBody.description: Confirmation of successful image reordering. Indicates that position values have been updated and a product snapshot has been created.

operations.specification:
Perform a soft-delete on the shopping_mall_product_images record.

Queries the record by id and verifies the seller owns the parent product (via join with shopping_mall_products).

If no matching image exists, throw 404.

If image already deleted, return 204.

If seller is not authorized (not owner of product), return 403.

Set deleted_at to current timestamp.

If this image was the primary image (position = 0), query for the next lowest-positioned active image and set it as new primary (position = 0).

Create a product snapshot copy of the product's current image array (including the deleted image’s deleted_at timestamp).

Return 204 No Content on success.
operations.description:
Delete a product image from the seller's gallery.

This operation removes the specified image from the product's visible image gallery by marking it as logically deleted. The actual image file is preserved in dedicated immutable storage to ensure historical accuracy of product snapshots.

After deletion, the image is no longer returned in product image listings, but remains accessible for historical views and order reference. If the deleted image was the primary (first) image of the product, the system automatically promotes the next image in order to become the new primary thumbnail.

This deletion is executed atomically and triggers an immutable snapshot of the entire product's image state at the time of deletion, allowing future customers to view the product's exact appearance at the time of purchase.

Only authenticated sellers who own the product can perform this action. The operation follows REST conventions for resource deletion, returning 204 No Content on success. No response payload is returned as the operation is purely idempotent and status-based.

operations.description:
Create a new variant for an existing product.

This operation allows a seller to add a new SKU configuration (e.g., different color, size, or option set) to a product that already exists on the platform. Each variant represents a unique product configuration with its own SKU code, optional price override, and specific option values (such as {"color": "Red", "size": "Large"}). The system strictly enforces that the SKU code must be unique across all variants of the same product and that the variant's product cannot have been deleted or suspended.

The variant's stock quantity is initialized to zero upon creation, and inventory adjustments are tracked separately through the inventory_logs table. Changes to the product's variant list trigger a product snapshot preserving the complete state of the product and its variants at the moment of change. This ensures that historical orders always reflect the accurate product configuration at time of purchase, regardless of subsequent edits.

This endpoint is accessible only to authenticated sellers who own the product. It does not allow bulk creation; each variant must be created individually. The request body must include at least one option value. If the product is not owned by the authenticated seller, or if the SKU code conflicts with an existing variant of this product, the request will fail with a 409 Conflict error.

Calls to this endpoint are automatically logged and audited. All variant creation events are captured in the product's immutable history, enabling administrators to reconstruct the product's evolution over time.

This operation depends on the following prerequisite: The product ID provided must belong to a product that is active (not deleted), owned by the authenticated seller, and has a status of 'approved' or 'active'. If the product does not meet these criteria, the request will be denied.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_products to verify existence and ownership of the product by the authenticated seller. Validate that the product is active (deleted_at is null) and approved. Check for duplicate SKU in shopping_mall_product_variants where product_id = productId and sku_code = request.sku_code, excluding variants with deleted_at. Create new shopping_mall_product_variant with received fields, setting created_at/updated_at to now, stock_quantity to 0, and deleted_at to null. Generate a unique variant_id (UUID). Within one transaction, create a shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshot record with all variant fields and action type 'create'. Then, update the parent shopping_mall_product with updated_at = now and create a snapshot of the full product state including the newly added variant in the variant_snapshots array. Log the event in admin audit trail with actor, timestamp, and product_id. Return the created variant object with full details including id, created_at, updated_at.

responseBody.description: The newly created product variant with all its properties including id, sku_code, price, and option values.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product to which this variant belongs. Must be a valid UUID and owned by the authenticated seller.
parameters.name: productId

requestBody.description: Details required to create a new product variant, including unique SKU code, optional price override, and option values in JSON format.

prerequisites.description: Product must be created and approved before variants can be added to it. The product ID in the path parameter must reference a valid, active, approved product.

operations.description:
Update an existing product variant's SKU code, price, or option values.

This endpoint allows sellers to modify the specifications of a product variant, such as changing its SKU code, adjusting its price, or updating its option values (e.g., color or size). All changes trigger the creation of an immutable product-snapshot-SKV record that preserves the exact state of the variant before modification. This ensures historical accuracy for order fulfillment and dispute resolution, in accordance with the platform's snapshot principle.

The variant being updated must not be referenced by any order items with status "paid" or "shipped", as this would violate the integrity of committed transactions. If such order items exist, the operation will fail with a 409 Conflict response. The SKU code must remain unique across all variants on the entire platform to prevent ambiguity in inventory management. Any modification of variant options (e.g., changing "color: Red" to "color: Blue") is treated as a structural change and requires a new snapshot, allowing customers and administrators to trace the variant's evolution.

All changes are logged with the seller ID and timestamp, ensuring accountability. This endpoint does not support mass updates or batch operations; each variant must be updated individually. For bulk changes, sellers should use the variant management dashboard, which triggers individual calls to this endpoint in sequence.

The operation does not affect inventory or stock levels. Stock adjustments must be performed via dedicated inventory endpoints. The variant's parent product must be active; if the product is deleted, this endpoint will return a 404 Not Found. The system implements soft deletion via the deleted_at column — the variant remains in database history but is marked inactive and becomes unavailable for new purchases.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Retrieve variant by variantId and productId. Validate seller owns variant. Check if variant has any order items with status 'paid' or 'shipped' via shopping_mall_order_items. If found, return 409 Conflict with error code 'VARIANT_IN_USE'. Validate SKU uniqueness across all shopping_mall_product_variants. Validate option_values format as JSON object. If any field (sku_code, price, option_values) is provided, create new shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots record with current state as previous values. Update shopping_mall_product_variants record with new values and update_at timestamp. Return 200 OK with updated variant object including new values.

responseBody.description: Updated variant details including current SKU, price, option values, and timestamps.

operations.description:
Permanently delete a product variant if no active orders, cancellations, or refunds are associated with it.

This operation performs a hard delete on the product variant record, completely removing it from the marketplace. The deletion is conditional and denied if any order items exist with status 'paid' or 'shipped', or if any pending cancellation or refund requests are linked to this variant. This ensures transactional integrity and prevents loss of financial accountability for completed transactions.

After successful deletion, an immutable reference to this variant's state is preserved in the shopping_mall_product_snapshot_variants junction table, linked to the product's current snapshot. This allows historical reporting and audit trails without preserving the live variant record.

All associated inventory records are permanently removed. The variant's original pricing and SKU data remain accessible through its snapshot record.

This API is only accessible to authenticated sellers who own the product. Admins cannot directly delete variants through this endpoint (they must use admin-level approval flows). Customers cannot interact with this endpoint.

Note: This operation does not delete the parent product. Products may remain in the catalog even if all variants are deleted, and will appear as 'unavailable' to customers.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Validate that the variant with variantId exists and belongs to productId (foreign key constraint). Ensure the requesting seller owns the product via JWT token verification.

2. Check the shopping_mall_order_items table for any records with shopping_mall_product_variant_id = variantId where status IN ('paid', 'shipped'). If any found, return 409 Conflict with message: "Cannot delete variant because it has paid or shipped order items".

3. Check the shopping_mall_cancellation_requests table for any records with order_item_id IN (SELECT id FROM shopping_mall_order_items WHERE shopping_mall_product_variant_id = variantId) and status = 'pending'. If any found, return 409 Conflict with message: "Cannot delete variant because it has pending cancellation requests".

4. Check the shopping_mall_refund_requests table for any records with order_item_id IN (SELECT id FROM shopping_mall_order_items WHERE shopping_mall_product_variant_id = variantId) and status = 'pending'. If any found, return 409 Conflict with message: "Cannot delete variant because it has pending refund requests".

5. If all checks pass, update the shopping_mall_product_variants record: set deleted_at to current timestamp.

6. Create an immutable record in shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots with all current variant fields (sku_code, price, options, created_at, updated_at) and operation_type: "delete".

7. Delete all associated inventory_logs records for this variant (shopping_mall_inventory_logs.variant_id = variantId).

8. Return the deleted variant's data in response body as IShoppingMallProductVariant for audit trail consistency.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the variant to be deleted.

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete immutable history of product changes for audit, compliance, and dispute resolution.

This endpoint returns a paginated list of all historical snapshots of a product’s metadata—including name, description, base price, and category—at the exact moment each change was made by a seller or administrator. Each snapshot captures the product’s state as it existed before modification, preserving the factual record for legal and operational integrity.

This functionality is central to shoppingMall’s principle of immutable audit trails, enabling customers to verify what was advertised at the time of purchase, sellers to prove their product descriptions remained consistent, and administrators to investigate disputes with unalterable evidence. Changes are versioned sequentially and always traceable to the actor who made the edit.

Responses include the version number, change timestamp, and actor (seller or admin), but do not include variant-level data or product images—these are accessible via dedicated snapshot endpoints for variants and images. The list is ordered from newest to oldest to prioritize recent modifications.

This operation is read-only and returns no data if the product does not exist or has never been modified.

operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_product_snapshots table filtered by product_id. Join with shopping_mall_users to get changed_by display name. Order by version DESC to show newest versions first. Apply pagination with page and limit parameters. Return only fields: version, name, description, base_price, category_id, changed_at, changed_by_id, and snapshot_id. Do not include variant snapshots or product images in this response—they are accessible via separate linked endpoints. Use immutable snapshot records only—no live product data.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of immutable product snapshot summaries, ordered from newest to oldest.

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete immutable history of all changes made to a specific product variant.

This endpoint provides a chronological list of every version of a product variant's state, including SKU code, price, and option values, captured at the moment each change occurred. Each snapshot record contains the exact values as they existed at the time of change, along with the timestamp, actor who made the change, and previous values (if applicable). This comprehensive audit trail enables precise reconstruction of pricing and configuration history for dispute resolution, financial auditing, and compliance verification.

Customers may retrieve snapshots only for variants they have purchased in past orders. Sellers may view snapshots for all variants they have created. Administrators have access to all variant snapshots on the platform, regardless of ownership. This endpoint never returns live variant data—only historical snapshots maintained in immutable storage.

The snapshot data preserves every modification, including initial creation, SKU updates, price changes, and option value modifications. Even if the current variant has been deleted, its full history remains accessible through this endpoint.

This operation is critical for resolving customer disputes regarding pricing discrepancies, product configuration mismatches, or unauthorized changes. For example, if a customer claims they were charged a different price at time of purchase, the system can retrieve the exact variant snapshot from the order record and compare it to the corresponding snapshot in this history to verify accuracy.

Query shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots table filtered by product_variant_id and ordered by version ascending.
Join with shopping_mall_users to retrieve actor display name.
Apply pagination using page and limit parameters.
Apply authorization rules: return results only if:
- Actor is seller who created the variant
- Actor is customer who has purchased this variant in an order
- Actor is administrator
Return error 403 if unauthorized.
Return paginated response structure with data array and pagination metadata.

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete ordered set of active images associated with a specific product.

This endpoint returns all currently active (non-deleted) images for the specified product in the exact order set by the seller. Each image is represented by its public URL and positional index for rendering in product galleries.

Images are immutable artifacts; they are never modified or reordered directly. Any image reordering or deletion triggers the creation of a new product snapshot, and this endpoint always serves the current state of the active product.

Access is authorized based on actor ownership: customers can view images of products they have purchased or are browsing, sellers can view images of their own products, and administrators can view images of any product. Deleted images are excluded from results, in accordance with the snapshot principle that historical images are preserved only within product snapshots and not in the active product view.

Return only image_url and position fields. Do not join with products table — product_id is sufficient for validation. Return empty array if product exists but has no active images.

Retrieve all active variants for a specific product.

This endpoint provides customers with a complete list of available product configurations (SKUs) including pricing, stock availability, and option values (such as color, size, etc.). Only variants from approved sellers are displayed, and variants that are out of stock or deleted are excluded.

The response supports product browsing and selection in the shopping cart flow. Customers can compare different variants of the same product based on price and availability. Each variant is identified by a unique SKU code that is used for inventory tracking and order fulfillment.

Variants are immutable in historical orders through snapshots, but this endpoint only returns current active variants. Variant price overrides are displayed if set; otherwise, the product's base price is used as the default.

This operation does not return information about variant history or snapshots - for that, use the variant snapshot endpoint.

operations.name: at

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of products available on the shoppingMall platform.

This operation enables customers and administrators to search and filter products across the entire catalog using multiple criteria including text search, category ID, price range, stock availability, and sort order. The response returns product summaries optimized for list display, including essential metadata like name, base price, category, seller shop name, main image, average rating, and variant count.

Business rules enforced:
- All product listings respect logical deletion: products marked as deleted_at are excluded by default
- Inventory filtering: in_stock_only=true only returns products with at least one active variant having stock_quantity > 0
- Pricing: base_price reflects the current product base price, not variant-specific pricing
- Categorization: category_id filters products by their primary category; category hierarchy is not applied
- Text search: matches case-insensitive partial string against product name and description

This endpoint does not return variant details, full descriptions, or reviews. For detailed product views, use GET /products/{productId}.

Related operations:
- GET /products/{productId}: Retrieve full product details with variants and reviews
- POST /admin/products: Create new product (admin only)
- PUT /sellers/products/{productId}: Update product (seller only)
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_products table with left joins to shopping_mall_categories and shopping_mall_sellers. Filter by: deleted_at IS NULL, name/description ILIKE %search%, category_id = ?, base_price BETWEEN ? AND ?, IN (SELECT variant_id FROM shopping_mall_product_variants WHERE stock_quantity > 0) when in_stock_only=true. Sort based on: created_at DESC (newest), base_price ASC, base_price DESC. Paginate using OFFSET/LIMIT or cursor-based pagination. Include aggregated fields: AVG(review.rating) as avg_rating, COUNT(review.id) as review_count. For each product, fetch one main image (position=0) and count variants. Return only fields defined in IShoopingMallProduct.ISummary DTO. Exclude variants, images array, reviews array, and product descriptions in response.

operations.specification: Create a new product in the shoppingMall catalog under the authenticated seller. Validate that the seller is approved and the category exists. Ensure product name is 1-100 characters, description is 50-1000 characters, and base_price is ≥ 0.01. Require at least one variant with unique SKU code (3-20 alphanumeric characters). If variants are provided, validate each has valid option values. Store the product with active status and current timestamps. Create a product snapshot capturing the entire product state including all images and variants. Associate product with seller_id from JWT token. Return 400 if validations fail, 403 if seller not approved, 409 if SKU already exists. Product must not be marked deleted at creation.
operations.description:
Create a new product listing in the shoppingMall marketplace for sale by an approved seller.

This operation allows registered sellers to add new products to their catalog. Each product must have a unique name, detailed description, assigned category, and a base price. Products must have at least one variant (SKU), with optional price overrides and customizable option values (e.g., color, size).

When a product is created, the system automatically generates an immutable snapshot of the product's initial state — including its name, description, base price, category, and all variants — for future audit, dispute resolution, and historical integrity purposes. This snapshot preserves the exact state of the product at the moment of creation, even if it is later modified or deleted.

Only approved sellers can create products. Pending or suspended sellers are rejected. The product is immediately visible to customers upon creation and appears in category listings and search results, unless explicitly deleted. Product images and variants can be added or modified post-creation via dedicated endpoints.

This operation is fundamental to the marketplace model, enabling sellers to bring goods to market while ensuring transparency and trust through immutable record-keeping. All product data is preserved in its original form to protect consumers from misleading edits after purchase.

If a product is deleted, it is permanently removed from the catalog and cannot be recovered. Unlike soft-delete systems, there is no recovery mechanism or archived state.

Related operations:
- GET /products: Retrieve product listings
- PUT /sellers/products/{product_id}: Edit product details
- DELETE /sellers/products/{product_id}: Delete product (if no paid/shipped items)
- GET /sellers/products/{product_id}/snapshots: View historical versions

requestBody.description: Product creation data including name, description, category, base price, and optional variants and images.

responseBody.description: Success response containing the newly created product's unique identifier.

operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_inventory_logs table with pagination and filtering. Filter by variant_id if provided. Filter by reason (restock, order, cancellation, refund, adjustment, loss) if provided. Filter by date range (created_at_gte, created_at_lte) if provided. Optionally filter by reference_id. Return cursor-based pagination with 20 records per page by default. Sort by created_at DESC to show most recent logs first. Never include product or seller information in results since these are not stored in the inventory_log model. Calculate running total of inventory changes on the application layer by summing change_quantity field sequentially.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated history of all inventory changes for product variants.

This operation provides comprehensive audit capabilities for tracking stock level changes across the platform. Sellers can view the complete history of inventory adjustments for their own products, while administrators can search across all variants on the platform. Each record represents an atomic change to stock quantity with associated metadata including reason, timestamp, and optional reference.

The inventory history is immutable and append-only. Changes are categorized by type: restock (positive), order purchase (negative), cancellation refund (positive), refund (positive), manual adjustment (positive or negative), and loss (negative). No records are ever deleted or modified after creation.

Users can filter logs by product variant, reason type, or date range to investigate specific inventory events. The system does not calculate running totals — this is the responsibility of the UI or client application, which must aggregate change_quantity values from returned logs.

Include optional in_stock_only filter to exclude items with zero stock. Join with product_variant_snapshots to get current stock_quantity. Calculate item_total = quantity * unit_price. Return paginated results with total count. Include in_stock boolean flag derived from comparing quantity against variant_snapshot's stock_quantity. Do not modify any cart state.
operations.description:
Retrieve the current customer's shopping cart items with inventory and pricing details.

This endpoint returns a paginated list of all items currently in the customer's active cart, including the product name, variant options, unit price, quantity, and total value. Each item contains an immutable snapshot of the product and variant state as they existed at the time of addition to cart, ensuring pricing and description consistency for audit.

The operation supports filtering by stock availability: when in_stock_only=true, only items with available stock (quantity <= variant's current stock_quantity) are returned. This helps customers avoid attempting to checkout items that may be out-of-stock.

Each cart item includes an in_stock flag that indicates whether the current inventory levels permit the requested quantity. Items with insufficient stock are still included in the response but flagged for customer awareness.

This operation does not modify cart state. It is read-only and designed for cart display and checkout eligibility checks. For modification of cart items, use PUT /carts/{cart_item_id} to adjust quantities or DELETE to remove items.

The response structure follows the IPageIShoppingMallCartItem.ISummary pattern to support pagination, with a total count of matching items and a list of summary objects suitable for UI rendering.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of cart items with inventory status and pricing

operations.specification:
Create a new cart item or update existing (merge) if variant already exists in cart.
- Validate customer is authenticated (JWT required)
- Validate variant exists and is active (not deleted or suspended)
- Validate variant has available stock > 0
- Validate seller account is not suspended
- Validate quantity is ≥1 and ≤50
- If cart item with same variant_id exists for customer:
  - Update quantity: existing_quantity + requested_quantity
  - Validate new total ≤ available stock
- Else:
  - Fetch variant and seller details
  - Create cart item with:
    - customer_id
    - variant_id
    - product_snapshot_id
    - variant_snapshot_id
    - seller_id
    - quantity (as requested)
    - unit_price (from variant_snapshot)
    - item_total (quantity × unit_price)
    - created_at
    - updated_at
    - deleted_at: null
- Return created/updated cart item with full details
operations.description:
Add a product variant to the customer's shopping cart.

This operation allows customers to store items they intend to purchase later. When a variant is added, the system captures and preserves its exact price, SKU, and product metadata at the moment of addition, ensuring that price changes or product updates after this point do not affect the cart. This ensures price stability and transparency during the shopping session.

The system handles both new additions and quantity updates. If the customer adds a variant that is already in their cart, the system merges the quantities rather than creating a duplicate. All cart modifications are immediately validated against current inventory levels and seller status.

This endpoint is exclusive to authenticated customers. The cart serves as a temporary container and does not constitute a purchase—inventory is not deducted until checkout. During checkout, cart items are converted into immutable order items.

To add an item, the client must provide the variant ID and desired quantity. The quantity is limited to 50 units per item. If the requested quantity exceeds available stock, the request fails with an appropriate error message. Multiple items can be added sequentially by calling this endpoint for each variant.

Related operations:
- GET /cart — view current cart contents
- PUT /cart/{cart_item_id} — update quantity of existing cart item
- DELETE /cart/{cart_item_id} — remove an item from cart
- POST /checkout — convert cart to order and deduct inventory

requestBody.description: The variant ID and quantity to be added to the cart.

responseBody.description: The created or updated cart item with its unique ID and final quantity.

operations.name: create

operations.description:
Update the quantity of a specific cart item for the authenticated customer.

This operation modifies the quantity of an existing cart item, performing strict validation against the variant's current stock level. The system will reject any request attempting to set a quantity less than 1 or greater than the available stock. Only the quantity field is modifiable; the variant, product, and seller information remain fixed as captured at time of cart addition.

If the requested quantity exceeds stock availability, the system returns a 409 Conflict status with an error message detailing the available stock. Quantity reductions to 0 are treated as item removal, and the cart item is deleted entirely. All updates trigger a recalculation of the cart's total quantity and total value.

This endpoint is not intended for batch updates. To update multiple items simultaneously, the client must make individual requests for each cart item.

This operation is protected and requires a valid customer authentication token. Unauthenticated requests will receive a 401 Unauthorized response. Additionally, a customer may only modify their own cart items; attempts to update another customer's cart item will return 403 Forbidden.

This operation is tightly coupled with inventory management. The available stock is dynamically calculated from the variant's current stock minus any reserved quantity from pending orders or cancellations. This ensures customers only modify carts based on real-time availability.

If the variant has been deleted or deactivated after being added to the cart, the item becomes non-modifiable and will return a 410 Gone status. This reflects the snapshot principle: cart items are anchored to the state of the product at the time of addition, but still subject to real-time availability checks for quantity adjustments.

Modifying a cart item does not change the product, variant, or seller snapshots associated with the cart item — those remain immutable for audit purposes. Only the quantity field is updated in the cart item record.

Dependent on:
- GET /customers/cart — to view current cart state before update
- POST /customers/cart — to add new items
- DELETE /customers/cart/{cartItemId} — to remove items

The system enforces that all changes to cart items are atomic and tracked via updated_at timestamp for consistency and order snapshot generation during checkout.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update the quantity of a cart item by cart_item_id. Query shopping_mall_cart_items table for the record with matching id and customer_id (via authentication context). Validate that the requested quantity is an integer between 1 and the variant's current stock (from shopping_mall_product_variants). The stock is determined by: variant.stock_quantity - any quantity reserved in pending orders (via inventory logs). Reject if:
- quantity < 1
- quantity > available stock
- cart item is deleted (deleted_at is not null)
- cart item does not belong to the authenticated customer

If valid:
- Update cart item with new quantity
- Recalculate item_total = new_quantity * unit_price
- Update updated_at to current timestamp
- Return updated cart item object

Use transactional consistency to ensure cart item and inventory state remain synchronized.

Do not allow negative quantities.
If quantity is decreased to 0, delete the cart item record instead of updating it.
Log the update operation in audit trail if enabled.

responseBody.description: Updated cart item with new quantity, subtotal, and timestamp.

parameters.description: Unique identifier for the cart item.
parameters.name: cartItemId

requestBody.description: New quantity value to update. Must be an integer between 1 and variant's stock limit.

Do not physically delete the record. Preserve all snapshot data (product, variant, seller, pricing) for audit. Update updated_at timestamp.
operations.description:
Remove an item from a customer's shopping cart.

This operation performs a hard delete on the cart item, physically removing it from the shopping_mall_cart_items table. The system automatically preserves a complete snapshot of the product, variant, seller, pricing, and other relevant details as they existed at the moment the item was originally added to the cart.

This snapshot preservation is built into the design of the shopping_mall_cart_items table and ensures accurate historical record-keeping for order fulfillment, audit trails, and analytics—even if product details change after deletion.

Only the customer who originally added the item may delete it. This operation does not affect other cart items or the cart's overall state beyond this specific removal.

All order data returned reflects the immutable state at the time of transaction, including order totals, customer information, and shipping addresses as they existed when the order was placed. This ensures audit compliance and accurate historical reporting.

The system does not permit any modifications to order data via this endpoint. All order alterations must be performed through specific administrative action endpoints (e.g., /admin/orders/{order_id}/items/{item_id}/cancel).
