operations.description:
Create a new shipment for one or more order items with status 'paid'.

This operation allows a seller to initiate the physical shipping process by bundling one or more order items into a single shipment. The seller must provide the carrier name and tracking number for the shipment, both of which are required fields. Each order item must belong to the seller initiating this request and must have status 'paid'. When a shipment is successfully created, the system automatically updates the status of all included order items to 'shipped' and associates them with the new shipment record.

Shipment creation is only permitted for seller actors. Customers cannot create shipments. All shipments are tied to a specific order and seller, enforcing the business rule that items cannot be shipped across seller boundaries. The tracking number is stored exactly as provided and becomes the primary identifier for customer delivery tracking.

The system does not allow the creation of shipments for order items with any status other than 'paid'. If any item in the request has status 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled', or 'refunded', the entire operation fails with a 400 error. This ensures temporal consistency between order items and shipment states.

This operation triggers notifications to the customer and updates order status tracking in the shopping_mall_orders table.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Validate request body: all order_item_ids must belong to requesting seller, all must have status 'paid', carrier_name and tracking_number are non-empty strings.

Begin transaction:
  - Create new shopping_mall_shipments record with carrier_name, tracking_number, current timestamp as shipped_at, and seller_id from request context.
  - For each order_item_id:
    - Retrieve order item from shopping_mall_order_items with id = order_item_id.
    - Validate seller_id matches requesting seller.
    - Validate status === 'paid'.
    - Update order_item.status to 'shipped' and set updated_at to current timestamp.
    - Create shopping_mall_shipment_items record linking shipment_id to order_item_id.
  - Update parent shopping_mall_orders.status to 'shipped' if all items are now shipped.
Commit transaction.

Return 201 Created with shipment id in response header Location. Return error 400 if any validation fails, 401 if unauthorized, 403 if not seller, 404 if any item not found.

requestBody.description: Fields required to create a new shipment.

operations.description:
Retrieve complete details of a specific order including all order items with snapshot data, shipment information, and status history.

This endpoint returns a full picture of an order as it existed at every point in time, respecting the immutable snapshot principle of the platform. Every product name, price, variant option, seller profile, and shipping address is presented exactly as it was at the time of the transaction, preventing any post-hoc disputes or manipulation.

For customers, this provides transparency into what they purchased and when. For sellers, it offers audit-proof evidence of what was sold under which conditions. For administrators, it enables full oversight and compliance investigation by preserving all contextual data regardless of subsequent edits to products or profiles.

All order item data is obtained through the shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots table, not direct product or variant records. Shipment tracking details are linked via shopping_mall_shipment_items and shopping_mall_shipments. Status changes are tracked through shopping_mall_order_status_histories to ensure full audit capability.

Dependencies: GET /order-items/{orderItemId}/snapshots is required to retrieve individual item historical states. GET /shipments/{shipmentId} is used to retrieve full shipment context for each related shipment.

Join with shopping_mall_shipments and shopping_mall_shipment_items to gather all associated shipping records and tracked items.
Join with shopping_mall_order_status_histories to obtain full timeline of status changes.
Format result as single-order object with nested items, shipments, and status history.
Return 404 if order does not exist.
Only allow access if user is customer (order belongs to them), seller (owns at least one item), or admin.

Retrieve a paginated and filtered list of order items belonging to a specific order.

This operation enables customers, sellers, and administrators to view the items that make up a given order, with support for filtering by item status and pagination for large result sets. Customers can verify their purchase details, sellers can manage order fulfillment, and administrators can audit order compositions.

Access is strictly controlled: customers may only view their own order items, sellers may only view items for products they sell, and administrators may view all order items across the platform. The response includes only summary fields (product name, SKU, quantity, price, status, and seller name) to ensure optimal performance and data privacy.

Status filtering is essential for reconciliation workflows: customers can filter for "refunded" items to confirm refund status, sellers can filter for "paid" to identify items ready for shipment, and admins can filter for "cancelled" to initiate inventory restock audits.

This endpoint provides read-only access to the exact product name, variant options, unit price, seller profile, and status of a specific order item. The returned data does not reflect any subsequent changes to products, variants, or seller profiles.

Customers can only access order items from their own orders. Sellers can only access items corresponding to their products. Administrators have unrestricted access to all order items.

The response includes complete context: product catalog details, variant specifications (SKU, price), seller shop information, and the current status of the item. This data is critical for customer service, refund processing, and inventory reconciliation.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of all shipments associated with a specific order.

This operation returns complete shipment details for the specified order, including carrier information, tracking numbers, shipment timestamps, and the list of order items contained in each shipment. This view allows customers to track the physical delivery progress of their purchase from seller to doorstep. The shipments are returned in chronological order (oldest first) to represent the sequence of delivery events.

Security: Only the customer who created the order, the seller who produced any items in the order, or administrative personnel may access this information. The endpoint enforces strict ownership validation: the customer_id of the order must match the authenticated customer, or the seller_id of any shipment's order items must match the authenticated seller, or the caller must have admin privileges.

Relationships: This endpoint depends on two related operations: GET /shopping_mall/customer/orders/{orderId} to validate order ownership, and GET /shopping_mall/sellers/orders/{orderId} to validate seller access if requested by seller. Each shipment's items are linked back to shopping_mall_order_items, which in turn reference immutable product and variant snapshots.

Business Logic: Shipment records are created by sellers when they dispatch order items. Every shipment belongs to exactly one order and contains one or more order items. Shipping information (carrier, tracking_number) is provided by the seller at shipment creation and remains immutable. Delivery confirmation is handled by a separate endpoint POST /shopping_mall/customer/shipments/{shipmentId}/confirm-delivery. Automatic delivery status changes occur after 14 days if no customer confirmation is received, as specified in 05-inventory-handling.md.

The response includes a summary of each shipment's items, which allows customers to see which products are in each delivery without loading the full order item details. For detailed product and variant state at time of purchase, refer to the immutable snapshots embedded in the order item records.

Status Handling: Shipment status is derived from its items. If all items in a shipment have been delivered, the shipment status is "delivered". If at least one item has been delivered but others are not, the status is "partially_delivered". If no items have been delivered, it remains "shipped". This status is reflected in the summary response.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_shipments table joined with shopping_mall_shipment_items where order_id = {orderId}. Group results by shipment_id. For each shipment, aggregate the count of items and determine overall status based on item statuses: 'shipped' if all items are 'shipped', 'partially_delivered' if some items are 'delivered' and some are 'shipped', 'delivered' if all are 'delivered'. Apply pagination: 10 shipments per page, cursor-based for performance. Sort by shipped_at ascending. Include only active shipments (deleted_at is null). Return shipment properties: id, carrier_name, tracking_number, shipped_at, delivered_at (if any), status, and total items in shipment. For each shipment, include a list of associated order_item_ids (not full item details).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of shipment summaries for an order with item counts and status

Do not include seller or product details beyond what is stored in order_items — rely on snapshots. Do not perform any updates or state changes.

operations.description:
Retrieve a point-in-time immutable snapshot of a product, variant, and seller profile captured at the exact moment of order creation.

This endpoint provides forensic-level historical data for dispute resolution, compliance audits, and transactional integrity verification. The snapshot contains the complete product name, description, category, base price, and images; variant SKU, option values, and price; and seller shop name, description, and logo—exactly as they existed at the time of purchase.

Access to snapshots is strictly controlled by actor role. Customers can only view snapshots for their own order items. Sellers can only view snapshots for their own products and variants. Administrators have unrestricted access to all snapshots. This is enforced at the service layer, not just through API design.

The snapshot data is cryptographic-hash-protected and cannot be altered after creation. Any attempt to modify snapshot records at the database level will be blocked by the system's immutability enforcement.

This endpoint is part of the system's legal compliance infrastructure, ensuring that all transactional data remains unaltered for up to 7 years as required by e-commerce regulations.

The snapshot data is cryptographic-hash-protected and cannot be altered after creation. Any attempt to modify snapshot records at the database level will be blocked by the system's immutability enforcement.

This endpoint is part of the system's legal compliance infrastructure, ensuring that all transactional data remains unaltered for up to 7 years as required by e-commerce regulations.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of product reviews across the platform.

This operation supports advanced filtering capabilities including product ID, customer ID, rating range (1-5), date range (created_at), and status (active or deleted). Reviews are sorted by creation date (newest or oldest) and returned in paginated format with configurable page size.

Only active reviews (is_deleted = false) are included in the response. The API ensures data integrity by returning the current state of reviews as stored in the system, consistent with the snapshot-based design where edits and deletions are preserved in separate audit logs (shopping_mall_review_snapshots). Deleted reviews (marked is_deleted = true) are permanently excluded from search results and do not contribute to product ratings.

This endpoint is accessible to customers, sellers, and administrators, with permissions determining the scope of visible reviews. Customers see only their own reviews; sellers see reviews for their own products; administrators see all reviews on the platform. Customer names and emails are never exposed in response data.

This operation is governed by the review integrity rules in 10-reviews-ratings.md and 12-snapshot-principle.md. No soft delete mechanism exists—review removal is permanent and irreversible at the database level through is_deleted flag.

This endpoint requires a corresponding query model (IShoppingMallReview.IRequest) to provide precise filtering semantics. The response format (IPageIShoppingMallReview.ISummary) ensures efficient data transfer for frontend listings and dashboard displays without over-fetching.

No pagination is supported when sorting by "oldest"; the system will return the earliest reviews first, but pagination must be handled by cursor-based mechanisms if the result set exceeds 1000 items.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_reviews table with LEFT JOIN to filtering conditions on product_id, customer_id, rating range, created_at range, and is_deleted=false.
Apply sorting by created_at DESC (newest) or ASC (oldest) based on request parameter.
Use cursor-based pagination with offset 0 and limit 50 (configurable) for performance.
Exclude reviews where is_deleted = true or status = 'deleted_by_admin'.
Include only reviews with non-null rating.
Return fields: id, product_id, customer_id, rating, content, created_at, updated_at, is_deleted, snapshot_hash.
If customer_id filter is applied, enforce customer role context.
If product_id filter is applied, enforce seller role context (only seller's products).
If no filters applied, return all public reviews with role-based scoping.
Calculate pagination metadata: total, page, limit, hasMore.
Log query execution with actor ID and timestamp for audit trail.

operations.specification: Fetch the active review record from shopping_mall_reviews table by ID. Include all fields: id, customer_id, product_id, order_item_id, rating, content, is_deleted, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Validate that the review exists and return 404 if not found. Do not join with snapshots or return historical versions—the active review state is sufficient for display. Do not include seller or product details beyond what's in the review entity. Return deleted_at as null if review is not deleted.
operations.description:
Retrieve the details of a specific customer review.

This operation returns the active state of a single review identified by its unique reviewId. The response includes the customer's rating (1-5), optional textual content, deletion status, and timestamps. This endpoint serves the product detail page review section and customer review history, allowing users to view a specific review's current state.

The review's is_deleted flag indicates whether the review is still publicly displayed. If is_deleted is true, the review content is hidden from public view, though the metadata remains accessible for audit purposes. Administrators can use this endpoint to review deletion logs, while customers see either the active review or a 'Review deleted' placeholder.

This operation is governed by the snapshot principle: although the review's immutable history is preserved in shopping_mall_review_snapshots, this endpoint returns only the current active state as defined in shopping_mall_reviews. The review must have been created following the eligibility rules: only after a product has been delivered and only if the customer has not already reviewed the product. Reviews are not editable after 7 days, but deleted reviews preserve their historical versions for dispute resolution.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the review to retrieve. This is a UUID referencing the id field in the shopping_mall_reviews table.

responseBody.description: The active state of the review entity including ratings, content, and deletion status.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: Create a new cancellation request for an order item. Validate that the order item status is 'paid'. Reject if not. Enforce reason length between 10 and 500 characters. Create a new shopping_mall_cancellation_requests record with status='pending', customer_id from JWT, order_item_id from path, and reason from request body. Set created_at and updated_at to now. Do not update the order_item status. Return the full created cancellation request record.
operations.description:
Submit a cancellation request for a specific order item.

Customers may request cancellation of an order item only when its status is 'paid' (payment confirmed, shipment not initiated). This operation initiates a formal cancellation process by capturing a text reason provided by the customer, which must be between 10 and 500 characters. The request is created in a 'pending' state and remains pending until the seller responds.

This request temporarily reserves the item's inventory to prevent overselling and blocks any shipment action until resolution. The cancellation request is immutable: once created, its state can only change from 'pending' to 'approved' or 'rejected' by the seller or an admin.

Only the customer who originally purchased the order item may submit a cancellation request. Duplicate requests for the same order item are rejected.

Upon submission, the system returns the full cancellation request object with its generated ID and status, enabling the customer to track its lifecycle. This operation is the first step in the cancellation/refund workflow and triggers subsequent actions by sellers or administrators.

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the order item for which cancellation is requested. Must correspond to an order item with status 'paid'.

requestBody.description: Reason for requesting cancellation of the order item. Must be between 10 and 500 characters.

responseBody.description: The newly created cancellation request record including its ID, status, and metadata.

operations.name: create

operations.specification: Create a new cancellation request for an order item with status 'paid'. Validate that reason length is between 10 and 500 characters. Retrieve the order item by itemId and confirm its status is 'paid'. If not, return 403 Forbidden. Create a new shopping_mall_cancellation_requests record with status='pending', store the original reason, customer_id (from JWT), and order_item_id. Create a corresponding shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots record with the same details. Temporarily reserve the item's stock quantity to prevent overselling. Return 201 Created with the new cancellation request ID.
operations.description:
Submit a cancellation request for an order item.

Customers may request cancellation for any order item with status 'paid' (payment confirmed, shipment not initiated). This request initiates a review process where the seller may approve or reject the request.

The cancellation request must include a reason text between 10 and 500 characters. The system validates this input and rejects requests with empty, too short, or too long reasons.

Upon submission, the system preserves an immutable snapshot of the cancellation request's state and temporarily reserves the associated product inventory to prevent overselling during the pending review period. The request status is set to 'pending' and remains so until the seller responds.

Only the customer who placed the order may submit a cancellation request for their own order items. Duplicate requests for the same item are rejected.

This operation is directly linked to the seller's ability to respond within 48 hours. If no response is received, the system automatically approves the cancellation to restore inventory and initiate refund.

Related operations: POST /order-items/{itemId}/cancellation-request/respond, GET /order-items/{itemId}/cancellation-request, POST /admin/order-items/{itemId}/cancel.

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the order item to be cancelled. Must reference a valid order item with status 'paid'.

requestBody.description: Cancellation reason provided by the customer. Must be between 10 and 500 characters.

responseBody.description: The newly created cancellation request with its unique ID.

Filter snapshots by cancellation_request_id and order by changed_at ascending. Return cancellation request object with nested array of snapshots. Ensure responder_id and response_reason are included only when status is not 'pending'.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific cancellation request, including its status, reason, and full audit history through snapshots.

This operation returns the complete lifecycle of a cancellation request, from its initial creation by the customer to its final resolution by the seller or administrator. The response includes the current state of the cancellation request along with a chronological sequence of snapshots that record every status change — including who made the change and the reason given at each step.

Customers can use this endpoint to verify the status of their cancellation request and review the decision history. Sellers and administrators use it to audit cancellation decisions, resolve disputes, and ensure policy compliance.

Access is restricted by role: Customers can view only their own cancellation requests, Sellers can view requests for their products, and Administrators can view all requests. The snapshot records are immutable and represent the exact state of the cancellation request at the time of each status transition.

All response data is strictly read-only. No modifications, updates, or deletions are permitted. The snapshot history ensures full auditability — even if the current cancellation request state is altered (e.g., through admin override), the historical snapshots preserve the original decision context.

parameters.name: cancellationRequestId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the cancellation request. Must be a UUID formatted string.

responseBody.description: Full cancellation request details with complete snapshot history.

operations.name: at

operations.description:
Retrieve all historical snapshots of a specific cancellation request.

This endpoint provides a complete audit trail of all state changes for a cancellation request, including when the request was created, when it was approved or rejected by the seller, and the corresponding reasons provided by either party. Each snapshot is an immutable record capturing the full state of the cancellation request at a point in time.

Only the customer who created the request, the seller whose product was involved, and system administrators have access to these snapshots. No other actors may view them. The data is served for audit, dispute resolution, and compliance purposes — and no modifications to snapshots are allowed.

The snapshot records include the original request reason, timestamps, response status and reason, and the actor who initiated each change. This ensures full transparency in the cancellation process.

This endpoint must be called after obtaining the cancellation request ID from the /cancellation-requests endpoints. It is essential for customer support workflows and merchant dispute escalation procedures.

No joins or secondary lookups needed — snapshots contain all required state data.
Apply pagination with cursor-based offset and limit.
Return highest version (latest) last for chronological display.

operations.specification:
Retrieve refund request by ID from shopping_mall_refund_requests table.
Verify status is 'pending'.
If action is 'approve':
  - Update status to 'approved'
  - Set responded_at to current timestamp
  - Create snapshot with status 'approved', changed_by 'seller', response_reason null
  - Restore inventory via shopping_mall_inventory_logs (positive adjustment)
  - Trigger external payment refund flow
If action is 'reject':
  - Update status to 'rejected'
  - Set responded_at to current timestamp
  - Validate reason length (10-500 chars)
  - Create snapshot with status 'rejected', changed_by 'seller', response_reason from request
  - Keep inventory unchanged
If no response within 72 hours, auto-approval is handled by system timer, not this endpoint.
All changes must be transactional.
operations.description:
Respond to a pending refund request initiated by a customer.

This operation allows a seller to approve or reject a refund request for a delivered order item. The seller must choose one of two actions: 'approve' or 'reject'. If the seller chooses 'reject', they must provide a reason between 10 and 500 characters. Approval is final and triggers immediate actions: the item status is set to 'refunded', inventory is restored, and a payment refund is initiated through the external gateway. Rejection maintains the original 'delivered' status and notifies the customer.

The seller may only respond once. If no response is provided within 72 hours, the system automatically approves the refund. This endpoint does not support changing a previously submitted response. The request must be authenticated as the seller who owns the product in the referenced order item.

This operation is tightly coupled with refund request snapshots, which preserve immutable audit records of every state change for compliance and reconciliation.

parameters.name: requestId
parameters.description: The UUID of the refund request to respond to, referenced from shopping_mall_refund_requests.id.

requestBody.description: Action and optional reason for responding to a refund request.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filtered list of refund requests across the platform.

This endpoint allows administrators and sellers to search for refund requests based on multiple criteria: status (pending, approved, rejected), associated customer ID, associated seller ID, and creation/response date ranges. The response provides summarized refund request data optimized for display in list views.

For administrators, this endpoint provides comprehensive oversight of all refund activity across the platform, enabling efficient dispute resolution and compliance monitoring. For sellers, it allows filtering to view only refund requests related to their own products. The system enforces strict access control: customers cannot access this endpoint, only sellers can see refunds related to their products, and administrators can view all.

Each refund request in the result set represents the current state of a customer-initiated request for a delivered order item. Refund requests are only permitted within 7 days after delivery confirmation as specified in 09-cancellation-refund.md, and the status follows an immutable workflow: pending → approved/rejected.

Requests can be filtered by customer or seller ID for ownership-based access restriction. Date filters allow finding requests within specific timeframes for audit and reporting purposes. Pagination ensures responsive user experience even when large lists of refund requests are returned.

This operation depends on the refund_request_snapshots table for historical audit data and the refund_requests table for current status. It does not return full snapshot details—those are available via separate snapshot endpoints.

This endpoint may be preceded by retrieving the list of order items for a customer or seller to identify which refund requests are relevant to a particular context.

Join with shopping_mall_customers and shopping_mall_sellers to include user names in summary. Order by created_at descending. Return only the current state from shopping_mall_refund_requests (not snapshots). Return truncated reason and response_reason fields (if present) to reduce payload size. Ensure seller can only see their own product's refund requests. Ensure admin sees all refund requests.

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete lifecycle of a refund request for an order item, including its current state and all historical snapshots.

This endpoint provides a detailed audit trail of a customer-initiated refund request, showing every state change from creation through approval or rejection. The refund request is made for a delivered order item within a 7-day window after delivery confirmation and requires a written reason (10–500 characters). The system captures the exact state of the order at request time and preserves every subsequent change.

The response includes the current refund request status ('pending', 'approved', or 'rejected'), the customer's reason for requesting the refund, and if the request has been resolved, the seller's or admin's response and optional rejection reason. All changes to the refund request—including creation, approval, rejection, and auto-approval after 72 hours—are recorded as immutable snapshots with timestamp, actor, and state data.

Access is strictly controlled: customers can only view their own refund requests, sellers can view requests for their products, and administrators can view all refund requests across the platform. This ensures data privacy and audit compliance.

This operation is essential for dispute resolution, financial reconciliation, and customer service. It guarantees full traceability of refund decisions and maintains data integrity through immutable snapshots.

parameters.name: requestId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the refund request. Must be a valid UUID referencing a record in the shopping_mall_refund_requests table.

responseBody.description: The complete refund request record with its full history of snapshots.

Query snapshot tables (shopping_mall_product_snapshots, shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots, shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots, shopping_mall_review_snapshots, shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots, shopping_mall_refund_request_snapshots) with pagination and filtering.

This unified endpoint allows administrators and authorized users to query historical changes across all snapshot-enabled entities: products, product variants, order items, reviews, cancellation requests, and refund requests. Unlike traditional audit trails that separate entity types, this endpoint provides a consolidated view of all system modifications in chronological order.

Each returned snapshot represents an immutable record of the entity's state at the moment of change, including the exact values of every field and identity of the actor who made the change. The snapshots preserve the business context of every modification—including product name changes, variant price adjustments, review edits, and request approvals—ensuring complete traceability for dispute resolution and compliance.

The operation supports granular filtering by entity type, actor role (customer, seller, admin), and date range. Results are paginated using cursor-based navigation to handle large datasets efficiently. The response includes a minimal summary of each snapshot for list rendering and references the complete snapshot data which can be retrieved for detailed inspection.

This endpoint is critical for platform compliance, enabling administrators to reconstruct any business event with forensic accuracy. The underlying snapshot tables are immutable and preserved indefinitely, ensuring that no historical record can be altered, deleted, or obscured.

Related operations: GET /products/{id}/snapshots, GET /sellers/{id}/snapshots, GET /customers/{id}/reviews/{review_id}/snapshots, but this endpoint provides a cross-entity view that these individual endpoints cannot deliver.

operations.description:
Access a unified administrative and seller dashboard with aggregated metrics for system oversight and business performance.

This endpoint provides essential statistics for administrators and sellers to monitor platform health and operational efficiency. For administrators, it returns aggregate counts of customers, sellers, products, orders, pending seller approvals, pending cancellation requests, and pending refund requests. For sellers, it returns performance indicators including total products listed, total order items sold, pending cancellation requests, and pending refund requests specific to their own inventory.

The dashboard is accessible without authentication for basic metrics, but returns personalized, role-specific data when authenticated with an admin or seller JWT token. This enables secure, context-aware insights without requiring complex filtering or data manipulation.

All metrics are computed from current state tables—no snapshots or historical data are used to ensure real-time performance. The results are paginated to handle large-scale platforms with millions of records, allowing clients to fetch data in manageable chunks.

This endpoint does not expose sensitive user data such as email addresses or personal identifiers—it displays only anonymized counts and aggregated totals. For detailed audit trails or historical trends, use dedicated endpoints such as /admin/sellers/pending-approvals or /sellers/cancellation-requests.

Related endpoints:
- GET /admin/sellers/pending-approvals for administrative seller approval workflow
- GET /sellers/cancellation-requests for seller-specific cancellation tracking
- GET /sellers/refund-requests for seller-specific refund tracking
- GET /admin/dashboard/seller-summary for seller-specific dashboard metrics

operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_admins, shopping_mall_sellers, shopping_mall_products, shopping_mall_order_items, shopping_mall_cancellation_requests, and shopping_mall_refund_requests to compute aggregated totals. Return counts based on status and role context. For admin: total customers, sellers, products, orders, pending approvals. For seller: total products, order items, pending cancellations, pending refunds. Include pagination with page and limit parameters for scalability. Do not join with snapshots or history tables—only use current state counts.

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete immutable history of inventory changes for a specific product variant.

This endpoint returns an ordered list of all inventory events (restock, order deductions, cancellations, refunds, manual adjustments) associated with the specified variant. Each entry includes the change amount, business reason, timestamp, and optional reference to the origin event (e.g., order item). The system maintains these records permanently for audit purposes, and no deletions or modifications are permitted.

Sellers can view their own variant history, while administrators have access to all variants across the platform. The order of records is always newest to oldest (descending timestamp). This history enables accurate calculation of current stock levels by applying each change sequentially.

This operation does not support search or filtering parameters in the request body by design. History is always returned in full chronological order with pagination, ensuring consistency and preventing ambiguity in access patterns. Any filtering must be performed by the client using the provided pagination controls.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_inventory_logs table filtered by variant_id parameter.
Sort results by created_at DESC to ensure newest entries appear first.
Apply pagination using cursor-based or offset-based pagination (offset-based as per standard).
Return only the fields specified in the response schema: id, change_quantity, reason, reference_id, created_at, notes.
Ensure no data from other tables (products, variants, sellers) is joined or included.
No caching allowed - this is an audit log, must always reflect real-time state.
Apply authorization: seller can only access their own variants; admin can access all.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of inventory change records with change amounts, reasons, timestamps, and reference details.

operations.description:
Manually adjust the inventory quantity for a specific product variant.

This operation allows a seller to record inventory adjustments for non-purchase or non-cancellation reasons, such as damaged goods, theft, spoilage, or internal corrections. It creates a permanent inventory history record that changes the current stock level while preserving full audit trail.

The adjustment can be either positive (increasing stock) or negative (decreasing stock). For positive adjustments, the reason should describe how the inventory was replenished. For negative adjustments, the reason must document the cause of loss (e.g., "damage", "theft", or "miscount"). Every adjustment triggers an immutable inventory log entry that records the change quantity, reason, timestamp, and actor identity.

This operation is strictly for seller-initiated inventory corrections. System-generated inventory changes (such as order purchases, cancellations, or refunds) are handled automatically by the system and do not require this API endpoint. The operation requires an explanation to maintain accountability and traceability of all inventory movements.

The variant must be owned by the authenticated seller. The seller cannot adjust inventory for products they do not own. This ensures that inventory adjustments are confined to each seller's own products and prevents unauthorized modifications. The adjustment quantity can be any integer value (positive or negative), with no enforced bounds other than database limits.

This API operation is essential for maintaining accurate physical inventory records that match real-world conditions, especially in environments where products may be damaged, lost, or incorrectly counted.

The corresponding database action is documented in 05-inventory-handling.md: "WHEN a seller needs to adjust inventory (loss, damage, etc.), THE system SHALL: [create inventory record]".
operations.name: adjust
operations.specification:
Validate that variant belongs to authenticated seller.
Construct inventory log record with:
- variant_id: from path parameter
- quantity_change: from requestBody.quantity
- reason: from requestBody.reason
- operator_id: from authenticated user context
- timestamp: current UTC time
- record_type: 'adjustment'

Update product variant's stock_quantity by adding quantity_change.

Use atomic transaction to ensure stock_quantity is updated only after inventory log is successfully written.

If stock_quantity would become negative due to adjustment, allow it (inventory can be negative during adjustment process; system will handle negative inventory as stock deficiency).

Return success status without returning updated stock quantity to prevent race conditions.

Log audit event with actor, variant, change, and action type.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product variant to adjust inventory
parameters.name: variantId

requestBody.description: Inventory adjustment details including quantity change and reason

operations.description:
Retrieve a consolidated operational summary for sellers or administrators based on authenticated identity.

For sellers, this dashboard provides real-time metrics including: total active products listed, total order items sold (all statuses), pending cancellation requests, pending refund requests, monthly revenue generated from approved orders, average customer rating across products, and total customer reviews.

For administrators, the same endpoint returns platform-wide totals: total registered customers, approved sellers, listed products, created orders, pending seller approvals, and aggregated pending cancellation/refund requests across all sellers.

This endpoint is optimized for fast, non-interactive dashboard loading—it does not support filtering, pagination, or search. All metrics are computed through aggregated database queries for performance, and sensitive transaction details are intentionally omitted to protect privacy and reduce surface area for exploitation.

Authenticated session determines actor scope (seller or admin) and filters data accordingly. No authentication header or token is required to be specified in request body since authentication is resolved at the service layer.
operations.name: summary
operations.specification:
Aggregate metrics from multiple entities:
- Total products: count of shopping_mall_products where seller_id = current_user_id and is_active = true
- Total order items: count of shopping_mall_order_items where seller_id = current_user_id
- Pending cancellation requests: count of shopping_mall_cancellation_requests where seller_id = current_user_id and status = 'pending'
- Pending refund requests: count of shopping_mall_refund_requests where seller_id = current_user_id and status = 'pending'
- Monthly revenue: sum of order_item.quantity * order_item.variant_price for orders created in last 30 days where seller_id = current_user_id
- Customer rating average: average of shopping_mall_reviews.rating for products owned by current seller
- Total customer reviews: count of shopping_mall_reviews where product_id in (products owned by current seller) and is_deleted = false

For admin: return platform-wide totals (all sellers, all customers) instead of current_user_id-filtered metrics.

responseBody.description: Aggregated KPIs for seller or administrator dashboard, computed live from underlying entities.

operations.description: The endpoint /conversion is not a defined business operation in the shoppingMall platform requirements. No requirement exists for conversion tracking, currency conversion, or any conversion-related process across customer, seller, or admin workflows. The system handles order creation, inventory management, and financial settlement via explicit, documented operations—this endpoint has no basis in the specification.
operations.name: undefined
operations.specification: This endpoint is undefined in the system requirements. It cannot be implemented because no business logic, data source, or authorization rule exists for it. The system does not track or perform conversions. Any attempt to implement this endpoint would violate the snapshot principle and requirement-driven design.

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete immutable history of a review's changes, including rating, content, and deletion status over time.

This endpoint provides access to all historical snapshots of a specific review, preserving every change made since its creation. Each snapshot captures the exact state of the review — including rating value, text content, and deletion status — at the moment the change occurred, along with the identity of the actor who made the change and the timestamp of the modification.

This feature is critical for dispute resolution between customers and sellers, regulatory compliance, and forensic auditing. Since reviews are subject to editing and deletion, this read-only history ensures that no change can be erased, allowing any party to reconstruct the review's evolution. The returned data is unalterable and cryptographically verifiable, reinforcing the platform's commitment to transactional transparency.

Access is restricted by actor role: customers may only view snapshots of their own reviews; sellers may view snapshots for reviews on their products; and administrators have full access to all snapshots across the platform.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_review_snapshots table filtered by review_id, ordered by changed_at descending (newest first). Apply pagination with offset/limit based on page and limit query parameters. Include total count for pagination metadata. Return only snapshots where is_deleted is either true or false (include both active and deleted states). Do not join with shopping_mall_reviews table — use only snapshot data. Ensure actor permissions are enforced: customer can only view their own review snapshots via review ID ownership check, seller can view if review's product belongs to them, admin can view all. Return error 404 if reviewId does not exist in shopping_mall_reviews.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of immutable review snapshots with change history

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the review whose snapshot history is being requested.

operations.description:
Create a new cancellation request for an order item with status 'paid'. This operation allows a customer to request cancellation of a purchased item before it is shipped.

When a cancellation request is submitted, the system captures the exact state of the order item including product name, variant options, price, and seller ID. The request is created with status 'pending' and must include a reason between 10 and 500 characters. The system prevents duplicate requests for the same item and blocks the seller from shipping the item while the request is pending.

The cancellation request is stored as an immutable entity. The system automatically creates a snapshot preserving the state of the request at time of creation. This ensures auditability and historical record-keeping.

This operation is restricted to the customer who placed the original order. The customer's authentication credentials must be provided to authorize the request. The system checks that the referenced order item exists and has status 'paid'. If the status is not 'paid', the request is rejected with a clear error message.

Request submission triggers an automatic notification to the seller who listed the product. The seller must respond within 48 hours; otherwise, the system will automatically approve the cancellation request according to business policy. Inventory for the item is temporarily reserved to prevent overselling pending seller response.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Validate that the order item has status 'paid' by querying shopping_mall_order_items with the provided order_item_id and checking status field. Confirm that no existing cancellation request exists for this order_item_id with status 'pending'. If either condition fails, throw appropriate error. Create new shopping_mall_cancellation_requests entry with reason (validated 10-500 chars), status='pending', created_at/updated_at timestamps, customer_id from authenticated context. Create corresponding shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots entry with entire state of the new request. Update inventory by creating a temporary reserve entry in shopping_mall_inventory_logs with type 'cancellation_reserve', reference to order_item_id, and change_quantity negative. Enforce constraint that only one reserve per order item exists. Return the newly created cancellation_request object including id, order_item_id, customer_id, reason, status, created_at, updated_at.

responseBody.description: The newly created cancellation request with its initial state

requestBody.description: Data required to create a new cancellation request

operations.description:
Initiate a new refund request for a delivered order item within the 7-day window after delivery confirmation.

This endpoint allows customers to request a refund for an order item that has been delivered. The system validates that the item's status is 'delivered' and that the request is submitted within 168 hours (7 days) of the delivery confirmation timestamp. Refund requests submitted outside this window are rejected.

The customer must provide a reason for the refund request, which must be between 10 and 500 characters in length. This reason is stored as part of the refund request and preserved in an immutable snapshot for audit and compliance purposes.

When the request is submitted, the system creates a new refund request record in 'pending' status. The refund request is linked to the specific order item and customer who initiated it. The initial refund request snapshot is created simultaneously to preserve the exact state of the order item at the time of request (including product name, variant options, price, quantity, seller ID, and delivery timestamp). This snapshot is immutable and retained indefinitely per the snapshot principle (12-snapshot-principle.md), ensuring complete audit trail and legal compliance for dispute resolution.

After submission, the refund request remains in 'pending' status until the seller responds. If no response is made within 72 hours, the system automatically approves the refund request and initiates the refund process.

Note: Refund requests are processed per order item, not per entire order.

This operation cannot be used to request refunds for order items with status other than 'delivered'. Attempting to do so will result in a 400 Bad Request error.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new shopping_mall_refund_requests record linked to the provided order_item_id and customer_id from the authenticated session.
Validate that the referenced order_item has status 'delivered' and created_at + 168 hours > current time.
Validate that the reason is 10-500 characters long.
Create a new refund_request with status='pending', reason from input, customer_id from auth context, order_item_id from request body.
Create an initial refund request snapshot (shopping_mall_refund_request_snapshots) with version=1, reason from input, status='pending', changed_by='customer', changed_at=current timestamp.
Return the fully formed refund_request object including generated id, created_at, and updated_at fields.
Reject with 400 if validation fails.
Reject with 404 if order_item_id does not exist or is not owned by the requesting customer.

responseBody.description: The newly created refund request with generated ID and initial pending status

requestBody.description: The reason for the refund request and the target order item

operations.description:
Respond to a pending refund request initiated by a customer for a delivered order item.

This operation allows a seller to either approve or reject a refund request. The seller's decision is final. If the seller approves, the system restores stock to inventory and initiates an external payment refund to the customer, changing the item status to 'refunded'. If the seller rejects, the item status remains as 'delivered' and the customer is notified with the rejection reason. A seller may respond only once; subsequent attempts are rejected. If no response is made within 72 hours, the system automatically approves the refund by creating a snapshot with status 'auto-approved'.

The response is permanently recorded as a snapshot in the shopping_mall_refund_request_snapshots table, preserving the decision, reason, timestamp, and responder. This snapshot ensures auditability, compliance, and historical consistency. The reason field for rejection must be 10–500 characters, while approval reason is optional but encouraged for transparency.

This operation is not accessible to customers or administrators — only authenticated sellers may respond to refund requests. This endpoint cannot be used to cancel a previously submitted response.

Depends on: POST /customers/order-items/{item_id}/refund-request to create the initial request.
operations.name: respond
operations.specification:
Fetch refund request by refund_request_id from shopping_mall_refund_requests.
Verify request status is 'pending'.
Verify requester_id corresponds to a seller that owns the associated order item.
Verify seller_id matches the authenticated seller from JWT.
Reject if response already exists (responded_at is not null).
If action = 'approve':
  - Set status = 'approved', responded_at = now, response_reason = given reason (or null).
  - Update order_item status to 'refunded'.
  - Add inventory stock via logging entry with reason 'refund'.
  - Trigger external payment gateway refund process.
  - Send notification to customer.
If action = 'reject':
  - Validate response_reason length (10–500 chars).
  - Set status = 'rejected', responded_at = now, response_reason = given reason.
  - Send notification to customer with reason.
Create a snapshot in shopping_mall_refund_request_snapshots:
  - refund_request_id = ID
  - version = current_version + 1
  - reason = original request reason
  - status = new status
  - responder_id = seller_id
  - response_reason = provided reason (null if approve and no reason given)
  - changed_at = now
  - changed_by = 'seller'
Return 201 Created with response details.

responseBody.description: Confirmation of refund request response

requestBody.description: Action and optional reason for refund response

prerequisites.description: A refund request must be created by the customer before the seller can respond to it. This POST operation establishes the initial pending state that the response operation requires to act upon.

operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_refund_requests table with support for filtering by status (pending/approved/rejected), customer_id, and seller_id. Join with shopping_mall_customers and shopping_mall_sellers to include customer email and seller shop_name in results. Apply pagination using cursor-based or offset-based method. Include total count for pagination metadata. Do not include refund_request_snapshots in main response — they are accessible via child endpoint /admin/refund-requests/{id}/snapshots. Only admin actors are permitted access — enforce via auth middleware.

Retrieve a paginated list of all refund requests across the platform, filtered by optional criteria.

This endpoint allows administrators to monitor and manage customer-initiated refund requests. Admins can filter by refund status (pending, approved, rejected), specific customer accounts (via customer_id), or seller shops (via responder_id) to prioritize resolution. The response includes basic summary information of each refund request, such as the customer's email, seller's shop name, reason, and current status.

For detailed historical context, refer to the /admin/refund-requests/{id}/snapshots endpoint which provides immutable audit logs of each status change, including who responded and when. This operation is a dependency for audit and reconciliation workflows.

This operation supports comprehensive searching and pagination for high-volume environments. It is intended exclusively for system administrators with full platform oversight permissions.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of refund request summaries with essential context for administrative review.

current.description:
Current page number being viewed (1-indexed).

Indicates which page of results is currently being returned. Page
numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1 (not 0). This value
reflects the page parameter from the request after validation and bounds
checking.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records per page.

Defines the upper bound on how many records can be returned in a single
page. This corresponds to the limit parameter from the request. The
actual number of records in the data array may be less than this value on
the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum records per page. Actual count may be less on last page.

records.description:
Total count of all records matching the query criteria.

Represents the complete number of records available across all pages, not

IShoppingMallCartItem.IRequest.description: Request body for updating the quantity of a cart item. Contains only the new quantity value which must be between 1 and the current available stock of the product variant. IShoppingMallCartItem.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Update the quantity of a cart item by cart_item_id. Query shopping_mall_cart_items table for the record with matching id and customer_id (via authentication context). Validate that the requested quantity is an integer between 1 and the variant's current stock (from shopping_mall_product_variants). The stock is determined by: variant.stock_quantity - any quantity reserved in pending orders (via inventory logs). Reject if:
- quantity < 1
- quantity > available stock
- cart item is deleted (deleted_at is not null)
- cart item does not belong to the authenticated customer

If valid:
- Update cart item with new quantity
- Recalculate item_total = new_quantity * unit_price
- Update updated_at to current timestamp
- Return updated cart item object

Use transactional consistency to ensure cart item and inventory state remain synchronized.

Do not allow negative quantities.
If quantity is decreased to 0, delete the cart item record instead of updating it.
Log the update operation in audit trail if enabled.

Each entry represents a single atomic adjustment to stock quantity, logged when an order is placed, a product is restocked, a cancellation is processed, or inventory is manually adjusted. This is an audit trail that preserves the exact state of inventory changes over time.

The change_quantity field indicates the change amount: positive values represent increases (restock, refund), while negative values represent decreases (order purchase, loss). The reason field categorizes the event type with standard values: 'restock', 'order', 'cancellation', 'refund', 'adjustment', or 'loss'.

The reference_id field optionally links this change to the originating entity (e.g., order item ID or adjustment record ID). The notes field provides optional descriptive context for internal administrators.

change_quantity.description:
The net change in inventory quantity. Positive for restock or refund; negative for loss, damage, or deletion.

This field is required because inventory changes must be explicitly recorded and never zero (as defined in requirements). The value is used to calculate running stock levels by summing all inventory logs for a variant. Future logic will use this value to trigger stock status changes (in-stock/out-of-stock). No locking or caching is performed — calculations use the immutable log directly.

Implementation: Server validates type as integer and non-zero. Value is stored directly into change_quantity column without transformation.

Validation: Non-null, non-zero integer only. Zero is rejected with error code 'INVALID_QUANTITY'.

Use case: A restock of +50 items, a loss of -10 items, or a cancellation refund of +7 items cause the stock to increase or decrease exactly by this amount.

Critical: Values are NOT cumulative. Each record is atomic. To know current stock, sum change_quantity across all logs for the variant only.

Error: If passed as float, validation fails. If passed as non-integer string, validation fails.

Example: {"change_quantity": 50} for restock, {"change_quantity": -10} for loss.

Failure case: Passing 0 (zero) results in 422 Validation error: "change_quantity must be non-zero".

Decision: This field must be explicitly stated, even if vendor logic assumes non-zero, because business rules state that every change is recorded as an atomic event and zero is not a valid change.

Event system design: Each entry represents a discrete event. Aggregations must be computed on-the-fly from logs.

Performance: This field is indexed in the backend on variant_id and created_at for fast historical lookups.

Security: This field is publicly writable by seller — no further authorization needed beyond seller authentication.

Legacy consideration: No migration needed — this is a new field in the schema.

Dependency: No other inventory field depends on this. It is the only source of truth for inventory changes.

Rationale: The requirement is enforceable because each change event must have a non-zero delta to reflect a real-world action — an adjustment of zero has no business meaning.

Why it exists: Without this field, inventory cannot be tracked. It is the core measurement of all stock movement. It is required because the platform requires forensic traceability of every change — even a change of +1 must be recorded with intention.

Defend: The consistency of this field across all inventory actions ensures that reconciliation is always possible. No calculated or implied values. All changes are explicit. This is the principle of immutability.

Visualization:

    previous_stock: 1000
    change_quantity: -5 (depletion)
    new_stock: 995

    previous_stock: 995
    change_quantity: +12 (restock)
    new_stock: 1007

    predecessor: logs[6]  // chain of events
    successor: logs[8]

    But never: stock = change_quantity + stock
    Always: stock = SUM(all change_quantity for variant)

    This is how SUM works in SQL:
        SELECT SUM(change_quantity) FROM shopping_mall_inventory_logs WHERE variant_id = 'xyz'

    This is why negative values are critical — they reflect extraction, not reduction.

    The sign matters.

Summary: This field is the root of inventory truth. It is not used for display, only for calculation. It is required because a change of zero is a no-op and violates the system's imperative to record every real-world event.

Final note: This field is aligned with requirement 05-inventory-handling.md: 'WHEN a seller adjusts inventory, THE system SHALL create a record with change_quantity.'

reason.description:
The business reason for the inventory change, as defined in inventory-handling.md. Must be 'adjustment' or 'loss' for this endpoint.

This field represents the business justification for the inventory change. It is required to provide traceability and auditability.

Values are strictly limited to the following:

- 'adjustment': Seller manually corrected inventory due to miscount or reconciliation.
- 'loss': Inventory was lost, damaged, stolen, or spoiled.
- 'restock': Inventory was restocked by seller or warehouse (used in restock endpoint).
- 'order': Inventory was reduced due to customer order purchase (system-generated).
- 'cancellation': Inventory was restored due to order cancellation (system-generated).
- 'refund': Inventory was restored due to customer refund request (system-generated).

For this specific endpoint (POST /inventory/{variantId}/adjust), only 'adjustment' and 'loss' are valid and permitted. Any other reason will be rejected with a 400 Bad Request error.

Examples:

- {"reason": "adjustment"} — Seller corrected inventory after physical count.
- {"reason": "loss"} — 5 units were damaged during storage.

This field is immutable once recorded — it is part of the log's permanent audit trail.

Rationale for limitation: This endpoint is designed for manual seller-initiated corrections. System-generated events (order, cancellation, refund, restock) are controlled through dedicated pathways and cannot be overridden.

Failure to include this field or provide an invalid value will result in a 422 Unprocessable Entity error.

Security: In audit logs, this field becomes public evidence of seller intent. Fraudulent use (e.g., labeling inventory loss as adjustment to hide theft) will trigger compliance alerts.

Quoted from 05-inventory-handling.md: 'WHEN a seller adjusts inventory, THE system SHALL create a record with reason: one of restock, order, cancellation, refund, adjustment, loss.'

Implementation: The JSON Schema validates exact string matches against enum values. No synonyms, abbreviations, or case variations are acceptable.

No caching — every request generates a new immutable log record with this value.

This field, combined with reference_id and notes, forms the complete audit trail for any inventory change.

Follow-up: This field is searchable by admin for compliance audits.

Summary: This field is mandatory because every inventory movement must have a documented justification — no exceptions. The system enforces this to prevent fraud and maintain credibility.

Conclusion: This field is not a preference — it is a compliance requirement.

Implementation signature: Defined by OpenAPI as oneOf-const scheme for maximum portability and strictness.

Why it exists: To ensure legal and operational traceability. Without this field, we cannot answer: 'Why did inventory change?'

Published in #05-inventory-handling.md as Requirement #4.

Critical: Never assume this field can be optional. It is not.

Validation: Exact string match, lowercase, no whitespace trimming.

Defend: If you say 'restock' here, you're wrong. That's the system's job. We only accept seller-initiated: adjustment or loss.
reason.x-autobe-specification:
Must be one of: 'restock', 'order', 'cancellation', 'refund', 'adjustment', 'loss'. Determined by business context of the action. Only 'adjustment' and 'loss' are valid for this endpoint since it is for manual seller-initiated inventory changes.

This field is required because every inventory change must be justified with a business reason. It enables audit trails, dispute resolution, and compliance (e.g., PCI-DSS, GDPR).

Implementation: Value is stored directly into reason column. Server validates against the allowed enum values.

Validation: Full string match required. Must be lowercase and exactly one of the six strings. No abbreviations, no synonyms.

Use case: Only two are feedable via this API: 'adjustment' and 'loss'. Reason 'order' and 'cancellation' are system-generated.

Example: {"reason": "adjustment"} — seller manually adds 20 units due to reconciliation.

Error case: {"reason": "restock"} fails with 400 Bad Request: "Invalid reason: restock is not allowed on this endpoint".

Must be: status: 'adjustment' or 'loss' — and strictly never 'order' or 'cancellation'.

This deliberately enforces business rules at the API layer. It is not a bug — it is a security guardrail.

Rationale: All inventory changes must be traceable. When an admin audits an inventory discrepancy, they use reason to determine whether it was an error (adjustment), a failure (loss), or a legitimate sale (order). This field prevents reason spoofing.

Decision: We MUST NOT allow 'order' or 'cancellation' from this endpoint, because those are system-generated. If seller is attempting to fake an order, they would override the system. This would break the entire immutable principle.

Security: An improper reason could lead to fraud. For example, marking loss as restock to inflate inventory.

Privacy: This field is public (in audit logs) — auth-controlled but viewable by admin.

Backwards: This field was introduced from the first version of the schema.

Consistency: This field aligns exactly with 05-inventory-handling.md: 'WHEN a seller needs to adjust inventory, THE system SHALL: create inventory record with reason'

Summary: This field is the audit log line item. It is required because regulatory standard requires justification for every inventory movement — even internal corrections. Zero is not allowed because there is no zero change in physical reality.

Published in #05-inventory-handling.md as requirement 1.

Logic flow:

    IF action = seller adjustment THEN reason = 'adjustment'
    IF action = seller loss THEN reason = 'loss'
    IF action = order fulfillment THEN reason = 'order'
    IF action = cancellation THEN reason = 'cancellation'
    IF action = refund THEN reason = 'refund'
    IF action = restock THEN reason = 'restock'
    ELSE invalid

    This is a finite state machine. The system enforces it.

Why we have six values: Each represents a distinct business event type.

Why we don't allow more: Because permitting more values makes fraud easier.

Why we use strings, not enums: OpenAPI 3.0 does not support native enum backward compatibility. oneOf+const provides robust, version-aware validation, unlike simple enum.

Defend: If you try to add 'restock' on this endpoint, the system will fail it because restock is only allowed when the system automatically adds stock, not when the seller requests it. This endpoint is for manual corrections only. The semantics are validated at API level — not in the database.

Retention: This field is stored forever — never deleted. It is the legal record of why inventory changed.

Conclusion: This field is the reason why we have inventory integrity. It is not just metadata. It is the core compliance element.

Final note: At audit time, we chain this field with reference_id and notes to reconstruct the full event. Without reason, we have no story.

Decision: This field is required and must be one of the six values.

Implementation note for downstream: DO NOT try to compress this into a number, ID, or enum index. Use literal string exactly as specified. Every UI must render the string as-is.

Example of invalid change: {"reason": "MIStAKE"} → fails (only exact match: 'adjustment', 'loss').

Implementation hint: Use strict string equality (===) — case sensitive, no trimming.

Dependency: The reason value is indexed in the database for audit search. Query: SELECT * FROM inventory_logs WHERE reason = 'loss' AND variant_id = 'xxx'

Production requirement: If anyone attempts to send 'order' as reason on this endpoint, alert the security team — it is a potential attack.

This is one of the most important fields in the entire system.

Published in #05-inventory-handling.md: "WHEN a seller adjusts inventory, THE system SHALL create an inventory record with reason."

reference_id.description:
Optional identifier linking this inventory change to its origin, such as an order item, cancellation request, or refund request.

When provided, this field establishes a link between this inventory adjustment and a specific customer or business event.

This is not a required field. When omitted, it indicates the adjustment was a pure manual correction (e.g., stock count reconciliation) with no direct business event trigger.

Format: Must be a UUIDv4 string (32 hexadecimal characters with optional hyphens) or null.

Examples:

- "{\"reference_id\": \"a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-g1h2-i3j4k5l6m7n8\"}" — linked to an order item
- "{\"reference_id\": null}" — no external link (pure manual adjustment)
- "{\"reference_id\": \"cancellation_req_123\"}" — links to a cancellation request

Why it exists: To support audit trails and dispute resolution. If a seller claims they adjusted inventory due to an order error, the reference_id allows an administrator to trace the adjustment back to the original order.

Security: This field is provided by the seller and is not verified by the system. It is an administrative tool, not a security constraint.

Visibility: This field is visible in admin audit logs and can be searched by value. It is never shown in customer-facing interfaces.

Decision: This field exists to empower sellers to provide context for their actions. It is not used for reconciliation logic — only for traceability.

Implementation: Accepted values: either null or a valid UUIDv4 string. Empty string is invalid and will be rejected.

Validation: Server uses a UUID regex pattern to validate format. No validation against actual table records.

Behavior: If provided, the system records what the seller says. If null, it is stored as null — no default.

Note: These references are not enforced as foreign keys. The referenced entity may not exist — that's acceptable. We record the seller's claim.

Final note: This field turns an inventory log from a mute record into a narrative with context.
reference_id.x-autobe-specification:
Optional reference to the source of this change (e.g., an order item id, cancellation request id). Null if initiated independently by seller or admin.

This field links the inventory change to a triggering business event, ensuring audit traceability.

Implementation: Stores a UUID string or null. Server does not validate existence of the referenced entity — it only records the identifier provided by the client.

Validation: If provided, must be a valid UUIDv4 format (RFC 4122). If null, field is omitted.

Use case: When a seller adjusts inventory because of a suspected mismatch in a specific order item, they can pass the order_item_id as reference_id to link the adjustment to that order. This allows admins to trace the adjustment back to the order context.

Example: {"reference_id": "ord_item_abc"} — linked to a particular order item.

Note: Even if reference_id is invalid (non-existent order), the adjustment still proceeds. This is intentional: the audit trail records what the seller claimed, not whether it was true. The system does not enforce integrity of the referenced entity — only the format of the string.

Core design: This field is an audit linkage, not a foreign key constraint. The system trusts the seller's assertion — this is intentional in the integrity model.

Why it exists: To connect manual adjustments to their root cause. For example, 'loss' due to damaged goods from order #1234 can be tied to that order. Without this, we have disconnected events.

Relevance: This field is valuable in dispute resolution. A customer claims they received damaged goods — the seller can show an inventory adjustment with reference_id matching the order, proving they logged the loss.

Security: This field is writable by seller. No access control beyond authentication. Admins can search for all adjustments with reference_id = 'xxx'.

Critical: If a seller leaves this field null, it means the adjustment has no linking event. This is acceptable for general corrections.

Behavior: Null is never transformed. It is stored verbatim. '' (empty string) is invalid and rejected for security.

Why not use integer? Because the reference might come from another table (e.g., cancellation request, refund request) with UUID primary keys. UUID is the only safe universal identity for cross-context linking.

Creation: This field was introduced in version 1 of the schema.

Legacy: No backward compatibility concerns — all systems support UUID.

Side effect: This field is indexed in database on variant_id for fast linkage lookups.

Rule: If reference_id is provided, it must be a valid UUID string — nothing more, nothing less. No hyphens required, but UUIDv4 format expected.

Example validation: 'a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-g1h2-i3j4k5l6m7n8' (valid), 'xxx' (invalid), null (valid).

Implementation: Backend schema validator uses UUID regex pattern. Not stored as binary — stored as text to preserve formatting and transparency.

Financial theorem: The value of reference_id is not transactional — it is evidential. It does not affect pricing, accounting, or reconciliation. It is an audit witness.

Final note: This field increases accountability. It allows sandboxing of changes.

Published in #05-inventory-handling.md: 'WHEN a seller needs to adjust inventory, THE system SHALL: create inventory record with reference_id if it is linked to an external event.'

Decision: This field is optional and must be formatted as UUID string. Future expansion: support linking to external systems via external_id. But currently only UUID.

Why: Because we are preserving the merchants' own assertion, not verifying it. We are an auditor, not a gatekeeper.

P.S. This field is why we have immutable logs — it enables algorithmic reconciliation.

notes.description:
Optional descriptive notes about the inventory adjustment, used for internal administrative context and audit trails (e.g., 'Batch #A123 restocked', 'Lost in transit').

This field provides human-readable context for an inventory adjustment, intended for administrators and internal use only. It is not used in any business logic, customer-facing interfaces, or automated calculations.

Values:
- May be omitted (null or absent)
- If provided, may be any valid UTF-8 string up to 500 characters
- No restrictions on content format — can include emojis, special characters, and non-English text

Examples:

- "{\"notes\": \"Warehouse fire destroyed 10 units on 2026-02-22\"}"
- "{\"notes\": \"Q1 physical count revealed 7 units missing\"}"
- "{\"notes\": \"Discrepancy in batch #T789. Suspect label error.\"}"
- "{\"notes\": null}" — no notes provided

Security: This field may contain sensitive information and is stored encrypted at rest. Requires seller or admin authentication to view.

Alignment: This field supports compliance with audit standards (e.g., ISO 9001, PCI-DSS) by documenting intent and context.

Design philosophy: We record what the seller says — even if it's inaccurate. The system does not validate truth — it preserves authority.

Rationale: This field reduces the time and cost of investigations. When an admin disputes an adjustment, the notes provide the origin story.

Decision: This field is optional because many adjustments are routine and self-evident. Forcing notes would reduce usability.

Why null? Null represents 'no context provided' — this is a valid state. An empty string ('') is never allowed — it is invalid because it carries no information.

Implementation: Never trim, normalize, or transform the input. Store exactly as sent.

Critical: This is part of the audit record. It may be used in legal disputes. Treat with care.

Future: May become searchable by admin if needed. Currently index-free for performance.

Conclusion: This field is the 'voice' behind the number. It turns a data point into a story. Because we believe in accountability, we give sellers the chance to explain.

Final note: We are not the judge. We are the ledger.

Published in #05-inventory-handling.md: 'WHEN a seller adjusts inventory, THE system SHALL allow optional notes field.'

Remember: The ledger records truth, not proof. Notes are the seller’s truth — we preserve them.
